sentences.text: Families facing cost-of-living pressures are being offered some help, or "breathing space" as Chancellor John Healey is calling it.
sentences.article_title: How the Budget affects you

sentences.text: The help comes as prices are rising faster than expected with annual energy bills in particular likely to increase by hundreds of pounds in January.
sentences.article_title: How the Budget affects you

sentences.text: Here's how the key announcements in the Budget affect you and your money.
sentences.article_title: How the Budget affects you

sentences.text: If you are living in a home in council tax bands A to D in England, you will receive a one-off £100 "Household Energy Payment" from January, funded by extra tax on banks.
sentences.article_title: How the Budget affects you

sentences.text: It will be paid directly into your bank account.
sentences.article_title: How the Budget affects you

sentences.text: Council tax bands are listed below - you can check which one you are in by looking at your annual bill or checking the government's website , external , although that was struggling to cope with traffic after the announcement.
sentences.article_title: How the Budget affects you

sentences.text: Administrations in Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland will receive the equivalent funding, and they will decide whether to introduce the same payment.
sentences.article_title: How the Budget affects you

sentences.text: This is designed to help with soaring energy bills, with some forecasts suggesting a typical annual bill could rise by £400 or so to £2,100 in January the saving will be only a portion of that.
sentences.article_title: How the Budget affects you

sentences.text: Although it's designated for energy bills, you can spend the money on anything you wish.
sentences.article_title: How the Budget affects you

sentences.text: The VAT cut on electricity bills, which was introduced in October, will also be extended to July.
sentences.article_title: How the Budget affects you

sentences.text: It was due to end in April.
sentences.article_title: How the Budget affects you

sentences.text: Healey announces £100 energy payment for millions and bank tax rise in first Budget Budget 2026: Key points at a glance The fee for connecting to your gas supply so called standing charges will be scrapped in England, Scotland and Wales, next year "or as soon as possible after", the chancellor said.
sentences.article_title: How the Budget affects you

sentences.text: These fixed daily charges will then be shifted onto the price you pay for each unit of energy.
sentences.article_title: How the Budget affects you

sentences.text: The Treasury calculates that 60% of households will save an average of £45 a year, with lower users gaining the most.
sentences.article_title: How the Budget affects you

sentences.text: But the saving will come after the projected big rise in bills in January.
sentences.article_title: How the Budget affects you

sentences.text: Higher users - in the biggest houses but also large, low-income families - will pay more than they currently do.
sentences.article_title: How the Budget affects you

sentences.text: The government wants to extend reforms to electricity standing charges later.
sentences.article_title: How the Budget affects you

sentences.text: The 5p "temporary" cut in fuel duty on petrol and diesel, introduced by Rishi Sunak in 2022, will be extended to July.
sentences.article_title: How the Budget affects you

sentences.text: It was scheduled to be phased out from January.
sentences.article_title: How the Budget affects you

sentences.text: It means drivers will still pay the levy at 52.95p per litre.
sentences.article_title: How the Budget affects you

sentences.text: Motor fuel prices have risen sharply owing to the continued impact of the Iran war on drivers, with diesel having recently hit new records when it moved above £2 per litre.
sentences.article_title: How the Budget affects you

sentences.text: The cost of filling a typical family car with diesel has gone up by around £30 since late February.
sentences.article_title: How the Budget affects you

sentences.text: A tankful of petrol costs about £23 more.
sentences.article_title: How the Budget affects you

sentences.text: The chancellor has scrapped his predecessor's plans to reduce the annual amount people can save tax-free in cash in Individual Savings Accounts (Isas).
sentences.article_title: How the Budget affects you

sentences.text: Rachel Reeves had wanted the policy to encourage personal investment in stocks and shares.
sentences.article_title: How the Budget affects you

sentences.text: It meant, from April 2027, if you're under 65, you would only be able to save £12,000 a year in cash in an Isa, rather than £20,000.
sentences.article_title: How the Budget affects you

sentences.text: But that plan has now been ditched.
sentences.article_title: How the Budget affects you

sentences.text: Instead, the government plans to create a new "Starter Isa" for first-time investors.
sentences.article_title: How the Budget affects you

sentences.text: If you have a large amount in savings, or if you fail to use the tax-free Isa allowance, then you will pay more tax from April.
sentences.article_title: How the Budget affects you

sentences.text: You do not pay tax on all savings.
sentences.article_title: How the Budget affects you

sentences.text: There is the annual £20,000 Isa allowance, and an annual savings income allowance (in other words, the interest received on a savings pot) of £1,000 for basic rate taxpayers and £500 for higher-rate taxpayers.
sentences.article_title: How the Budget affects you

sentences.text: But beyond that savings tax rates will rise by four percentage points to 24% and 44% respectively from April.
sentences.article_title: How the Budget affects you

sentences.text: Landlords could also pay more in tax.
sentences.article_title: How the Budget affects you

sentences.text: In analysis published on Wednesday, the Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR) said these steps along with measures over the past decade that have reduced private landlord returns "collectively risk leading to a steady rise in rents".
sentences.article_title: How the Budget affects you

sentences.text: Minimum wage rates will rise by 3.9% in April.
sentences.article_title: How the Budget affects you

sentences.text: For all workers, the ongoing freeze in the income bands , or thresholds, at which income tax is paid went unmentioned in the Budget.
sentences.article_title: How the Budget affects you

sentences.text: But it means any kind of pay rise could drag you into a higher tax bracket, or see a greater proportion of your income taxed than would otherwise be expected.
sentences.article_title: How the Budget affects you

sentences.text: Scotland has its own income tax bands.
sentences.article_title: How the Budget affects you

sentences.text: How much is the minimum wage going up by?
sentences.article_title: How the Budget affects you

sentences.text: The chancellor said this would be the case until at least 2030, as there will be a new Pension Tax Allowance, so pensioners with an income up to the value of the full new state pension will not pay income tax.
sentences.article_title: How the Budget affects you

sentences.text: The First Time Buyer Isa has been in the planning stages with the government for a while.
sentences.article_title: How the Budget affects you

sentences.text: Healey has confirmed that it is intended to replace the often-criticised Lifetime Isa.
sentences.article_title: How the Budget affects you

sentences.text: Separately, he confirmed the Your First Home equity scheme to allow first-time buyers in England to buy a new-build home with a deposit of 2.5%.
sentences.article_title: How the Budget affects you

sentences.text: It would provide them with a loan worth 20% of their property's value to help pay for the purchase.
sentences.article_title: How the Budget affects you

sentences.text: The government has made no changes to student loan rates - saying only that it is being "kept under review".
sentences.article_title: How the Budget affects you

sentences.text: There has been some backlash after the previous chancellor froze the repayment threshold for Plan 2 student loans, which were given out for just over a decade in England from 2012.
sentences.article_title: How the Budget affects you

sentences.text: It means the salary at which borrowers start paying back their loans is due to stay at £29,385 in April and remain there for three years – so graduates start repaying sooner and repay more each month than they would otherwise have done.
sentences.article_title: How the Budget affects you

sentences.text: Some announcements affecting your finances have already been made by the government.
sentences.article_title: How the Budget affects you

sentences.text: Some cities already have caps, and funding is being given to the devolved nations

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: Aerial footage shows train crash scene Two trains have collided in Spain just south of the capital Madrid on Wednesday morning.
sentences.article_title: What we know about the crash so far

sentences.text: Rail operator Adif says the incident occurred between a Renfe train and another of the Iryo company, which covers the Madrid to Seville route.
sentences.article_title: What we know about the crash so far

sentences.text: So far at least 68 people are confirmed to have died in the incident.
sentences.article_title: What we know about the crash so far

sentences.text: Here is what we know about the crash so far.
sentences.article_title: What we know about the crash so far

sentences.text: The two trains collided just after 09:00 (08:00 GMT) between municipalities Mora and Orgaz, and about 140km (100 miles) south of Madrid.
sentences.article_title: What we know about the crash so far

sentences.text: The accident happened when a high-speed train travelling from Madrid to the south of the country collided with another train that was apparently stationary.
sentences.article_title: What we know about the crash so far

sentences.text: The crash caused at least two carriages to fall down an embankment.
sentences.article_title: What we know about the crash so far

sentences.text: Broadcaster RTVE, quoting the transport ministry, said a Renfe train rear-ended an Iryo train.
sentences.article_title: What we know about the crash so far

sentences.text: Renfe is Spain's national state-owned railway company while Iryo is a private high-speed railway operator.
sentences.article_title: What we know about the crash so far

sentences.text: All train traffic on this line has been stopped at stations along the route, Adif said.
sentences.article_title: What we know about the crash so far

sentences.text: Renfe said services between Madrid, Ciudad Real and Andalusia remain suspended.
sentences.article_title: What we know about the crash so far

sentences.text: A passenger on board one of the trains told local media there was a heavy impact about 40 minutes into the journey.
sentences.article_title: What we know about the crash so far

sentences.text: Iryo said its train was "struck from behind" by a Renfe train "due to causes that are still unknown.
sentences.article_title: What we know about the crash so far

sentences.text: Transport minister Oscar Puente has said a computer failure led to the initial halt of six moving trains, including the two trains that subsequently collided.

sentences.text: Firstly, as expected, it was a much smaller Budget in overall tax and spending terms than plenty of recent ones have been.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Budget felt cautious despite its range of small measures

sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Budget felt cautious despite its range of small measures

sentences.text: There are more taxes for savers and landlords, for instance, and too for banks.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Budget felt cautious despite its range of small measures

sentences.text: When a government has promised, as Labour have, to not put up income tax, national insurance or VAT – the big revenue generators – they end up looking elsewhere if they conclude putting up tax is necessary.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Budget felt cautious despite its range of small measures

sentences.text: That runs the political risk of choosing particular sectors who might respond rather noisily.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Budget felt cautious despite its range of small measures

sentences.text: Think of the plenty of farmers who were incensed by the changes to inheritance tax Rachel Reeves was keen on.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Budget felt cautious despite its range of small measures

sentences.text: And there is a recurring sense of déjà vu in the language of the OBR.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Budget felt cautious despite its range of small measures

sentences.text: As for what happens, next, well, frankly, who on earth knows.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Budget felt cautious despite its range of small measures

sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Budget felt cautious despite its range of small measures

sentences.text: Mitigating the bad is arguably a noble political aim, but it costs money and potentially comes with little political upside.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Budget felt cautious despite its range of small measures

The reaction of the opposition parties, from a range of different political perspectives, amounts to a critique that this Budget was thin.

sentences.text: Amazon Prime Air is expanding to 500 US towns and cities Nature lover Ashley Schmidt no longer spends much time in her garden, in the Dallas suburb of North Garland.

sentences.text: "They emit this very annoying buzz.

sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Amazon says it is working to reduce the noise of its drone fleet Schmidt is one of a growing number of people living with the noise of drones dispatched by companies including Amazon and Walmart as they seek to speed up home deliveries.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Delivery drone services, not long ago a novelty, are becoming part of everyday life for many people in the US.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Among them, Amazon Prime Air is in the process of expanding deliveries to nearly 500 cities and towns, delivering items that fit into a space the size of a shoe box.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: It has also launched to customers in and around Darlington in the north of England.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Even in cities where noise is already a steady part of life, the sound of drones seems to irk in a particular way.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: While the steady passing of traffic might blend into the background, the sudden whine of a drone's rotors can pierce the everyday hum.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: The sound tends to be "particularly noticeable, even when overall sound levels are relatively low," says Antonio Torija Martinez, professor in acoustic engineering and psychoacoustics at the University of Salford.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Unlike planes, drones operate at low altitudes and may fly directly over residential areas.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: "They can expose communities that have not previously experienced significant aircraft noise, and who may therefore be more sensitive to changes in their local soundscape," says Torija Martinez.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: He points to research showing that people respond strongly to a noise when they consider the source to be "novel, intrusive or frequent".
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Rachael Field from Rhondda Cynon Taf has cancer of the tongue and been given around three years or less to live A terminally ill mum who has been given three years to live has been denied disability benefit despite being unable to eat, talk, dress or use the toilet independently.

sentences.article_title: Terminally ill mum who can't talk, walk or dress herself refused Pip payment

sentences.article_title: Terminally ill mum who can't talk, walk or dress herself refused Pip payment

sentences.article_title: Terminally ill mum who can't talk, walk or dress herself refused Pip payment

sentences.text: Rachael's daughter Kyra has set up a Go Fund Me page to try and help her enjoy what time she has left Field's family said repeated rescheduling of the assessment process caused delays, and that despite lodging an appeal several months ago, they are still awaiting an outcome.

sentences.text: Prime Minister's Questions focused on Andy Burnham's Brexit stance Andy Burnham has insisted there is "no confusion" over his position on the European Union, as he criticised the UK's current deal with the bloc.
sentences.article_title: Burnham insists 'no confusion at all' over his Brexit position

sentences.text: The prime minister said it was his "responsibility" to improve the deal, which was ratified in 2020, at a summit in Brussels next month.
sentences.article_title: Burnham insists 'no confusion at all' over his Brexit position

sentences.text: He denied he had shifted his stance since the Makerfield by-election when he promised not to "re-run" the Brexit debate .
sentences.article_title: Burnham insists 'no confusion at all' over his Brexit position

sentences.text: Earlier this week, he suggested he could call a referendum on the UK returning to EU freedom of movement, before No10 appeared to backtrack .
sentences.article_title: Burnham insists 'no confusion at all' over his Brexit position

sentences.text: Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch accused him during Prime Minister's Questions on Wednesday of failing to "respect" the 2016 Brexit vote.
sentences.article_title: Burnham insists 'no confusion at all' over his Brexit position

sentences.text: Badenoch said Burnham had created confusion and asked if he wanted a referendum on rejoining the EU.
sentences.article_title: Burnham insists 'no confusion at all' over his Brexit position

sentences.text: "There is no confusion at all," Burnham told MPs.
sentences.article_title: Burnham insists 'no confusion at all' over his Brexit position

sentences.text: "The government has a collectively agreed position, which I have set out today.
sentences.article_title: Burnham insists 'no confusion at all' over his Brexit position

sentences.text: "It is entirely consistent with everything that I've said, including in the by-election.
sentences.article_title: Burnham insists 'no confusion at all' over his Brexit position

sentences.text: "The red lines in our manifesto, including on freedom of movement, will stay in place firmly for the whole of this Parliament." Labour's 2024 election manifesto ruled out a return of free movement, single market membership or a customs union.
sentences.article_title: Burnham insists 'no confusion at all' over his Brexit position

sentences.text: Freedom of movement allows EU citizens to travel, live, study and work in any member country.
sentences.article_title: Burnham insists 'no confusion at all' over his Brexit position

sentences.text: It is a precondition of membership of the EU's single market, which enables goods, services and people to move freely between EU member states.
sentences.article_title: Burnham insists 'no confusion at all' over his Brexit position

sentences.text: Badenoch accused Burnham of having "opened his mouth without engaging his brain" over freedom of movement during "the chancellor's big week" as the Budget is unveiled .
sentences.article_title: Burnham insists 'no confusion at all' over his Brexit position

sentences.text: "It was miserable, regardless of which side of the debate you were on." Burnham said Badenoch was "speaking the truth" here and the country had suffered from low growth and insufficient control on migration as a result of a "harder Brexit than what was promised" in the 2016 referendum.
sentences.article_title: Burnham insists 'no confusion at all' over his Brexit position

sentences.text: "Where I am focused is getting a better deal for Britain, that is my responsibility, and I will lead from this despatch box over the next few weeks," Burnham said.
sentences.article_title: Burnham insists 'no confusion at all' over his Brexit position

sentences.text: At a summit in Brussels on 20 November, Burnham will push options for a reset of relations with the bloc on issues such as youth mobility, food, drink, energy and cooperation on illegal immigration.
sentences.article_title: Burnham insists 'no confusion at all' over his Brexit position

sentences.text: Burnham's comments at Prime Minister's Questions came as a letter emerged addressed to his Cabinet ministers, asking them to be "aligned and disciplined" around the summit.
sentences.article_title: Burnham insists 'no confusion at all' over his Brexit position

sentences.text: "It will not be appropriate for ministers individually to advocate for specific options or opine on the likely outcome of the process," he wrote in a letter on Wednesday.
sentences.article_title: Burnham insists 'no confusion at all' over his Brexit position

sentences.text: He said he hoped the summit led to "some important, concrete steps" and he would set out the next steps "to consider the UK's long-term relationship with the EU as part of our 10-year plan".
sentences.article_title: Burnham insists 'no confusion at all' over his Brexit position

sentences.text: "Both the UK and the EU have changed considerably in the 10 years since the Brexit vote," he said.
sentences.article_title: Burnham insists 'no confusion at all' over his Brexit position

sentences.text: "Any future relationship depends on practical arrangements that are realistic for both sides, and responsive to this new reality." Any "fundamental change" to this relationship "would be for the public to decide and a matter for the next Parliament," he added.
sentences.article_title: Burnham insists 'no confusion at all' over his Brexit position

sentences.text: Lucy Baxter said she had struggled to cope without heating and hot water, particularly with a one-year-old at home Residents at a block of flats in north-west London have been left without heating or hot water due to historic unpaid bills of £600,000, despite monthly payments being made over several years.

sentences.text: The unnamed celebrity is seeking an injunction, and his legal team told the first day of a trial on Tuesday that any publication would be "highly likely" to lead him to kill himself.
sentences.article_title: Unnamed celebrity accused of 'inappropriate sexual activities', court hears

sentences.text: They told the court that his drastic reaction was not because of any wrongdoing, but because of the fear of "trial by media".
sentences.article_title: Unnamed celebrity accused of 'inappropriate sexual activities', court hears

sentences.text: The man denies abusing "his power and position as a celebrity to contact and forge relationships with young women and teenagers to try to have sex with them", the court heard.
sentences.article_title: Unnamed celebrity accused of 'inappropriate sexual activities', court hears

sentences.text: The legal team for ITN and Guardian News and Media (GNM) told the court that the celebrity's "suicide risk" could be mitigated and there was no proper basis "to restrain the publication of public interest journalism".
sentences.article_title: Unnamed celebrity accused of 'inappropriate sexual activities', court hears

sentences.text: A medical report carried out for the court said inpatient treatment could provide "significant, but not complete mitigation of the risk", but that treatment, perhaps for months, had "a realistic potential to reduce the risk".
sentences.article_title: Unnamed celebrity accused of 'inappropriate sexual activities', court hears

sentences.text: The judge, Mr Justice Nicklin, said there was "significant public interest" in the proceedings and that "this is a difficult and important case".
sentences.article_title: Unnamed celebrity accused of 'inappropriate sexual activities', court hears

sentences.text: He added: "The court must determine it fairly, on the evidence and legal submissions." Nicklin will not determine the truth or accuracy of the allegations, only whether they can be published.
sentences.article_title: Unnamed celebrity accused of 'inappropriate sexual activities', court hears

sentences.text: He also urged the press and public not to speculate about the identity of the man, who is referred to in court as PPT.
sentences.article_title: Unnamed celebrity accused of 'inappropriate sexual activities', court hears

sentences.text: "The existence of online speculation, however confidently expressed or widely repeated, does not authorise anyone to identify, or purport authoritatively to identify, PPT in connection with these proceedings," he said.
sentences.article_title: Unnamed celebrity accused of 'inappropriate sexual activities', court hears

sentences.text: "Nor does repetition transform speculation into established fact." Sara Mansoori KC, representing the man, told the court that any publication "would have a potentially fatal impact".
sentences.article_title: Unnamed celebrity accused of 'inappropriate sexual activities', court hears

sentences.text: She added in written submissions: "This is not a case where an individual has spuriously raised 'mental health' concerns in the face of an impending publication that they do not wish to occur.

sentences.text: The operators of Newby Island landfill have been ordered to take action over odours Milpitas, an affluent city in California's Silicon Valley tech hub, has an odour problem.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: For decades, residents have had to endure rank smells wafting from industrial sites, among them a 342-acre landfill.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "When I first moved here, I could not open my window for over 10 years," says Chia-Ling Kong, an engineer for a tech firm who lives around half a mile from the dump.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: While things have got better in recent years, Kong says she and her neighbours must still contend with around "two or three hours of bad smells a day".
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Perhaps befitting Silicon Valley, the community is putting its hopes in technology.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: The operators of Newby Island landfill have been ordered by local authorities to use drones and install monitors to systematically track and measure the chemicals responsible for bad odours.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: They have also been told to automate the collection of landfill gases responsible for smells.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Kong is optimistic a data-driven approach will make a difference.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "Hopefully with this continuous monitoring, it makes it easier to pinpoint problems at the moment it starts." The operators of the landfill say they are committed to operating it safely and protecting air quality.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Just like in Milpitas, where Kong is part of a citizen's campaign against the odours, communities around the world are raising a stink about bad smells making day-to-day life miserable.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Sometimes a rubbish dump is to blame, or it might be a sewage treatment works, or a reeking factory.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: When the complaints start stacking up, resolving them is not always simple.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Many countries have no regulations in place dictating how to manage smells.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: In the US, for example, the Environmental Protection Agency does not regulate environmental odours as a pollutant.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: This leaves states and local governments to take charge of the issue.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Urban sprawl is often part of the problem, bringing communities closer to stinky facilities that may historically have been kept at a distance.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: This is creating more demand for technologies to monitor and prevent smells.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Odour consultant Micheal Bull says people are increasingly concerned about neighbourhood stinks.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "You're getting developments being built nearer to odorous processes… as land has become more valuable, there is also infilling," Bull says.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: He is speaking about his experiences in the UK, but it's a similar story in many parts of the world.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Bad smells from waste sites are among the most difficult to resolve The technologies used to tackle industrial pongs generally fall into three categories: they absorb odours; convert them into something less smelly through a chemical reaction; or burn them away.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Experts on fixing industrial odours say that the best technologies, when used correctly, can remove 90% or more of the target compounds responsible for smells.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: But this can be expensive and some operators opt for simpler and cheaper solutions.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: These include masking odours from landfill or sewage processing by spraying giant quantities of deodorisers.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Odour experts contacted for this article were dubious about the effectiveness of such industrial scale air fresheners.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "In my view they're not likely to change the odours," says Bull, who likens them to fabric conditioner.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Bad smells from waste sites – a common cause of complaints – are among the stinkiest and most difficult to resolve, according to Carlos Diaz, an environmental consultant based in Spain.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "Landfill is difficult to treat because you have a very large surface," he says.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: In some places at least, technology is making a real difference.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Residents in Des Moines, Iowa, have long complained of the so-called Eastside Funk, a putrid scent that residents report drifts over parts of the city.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: A study commissioned by city authorities showed that a trio of industrial meat companies were among culprits.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "Within 10 miles, there's about half a million people," says Dalton Jacobus, who works in the Department of Neighborhood Services.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "If the winds are out of the wrong direction, 100,000 people can be in the middle of that odour plume." The authorities are now paying around $240,000 (£182,000) a year on technology to track the stink, so they can take action.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "What we wanted to do was build a ring of odour monitors around the facilities that we suspected of emitting odours," says Jacobus.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: The monitors, which measure levels of chemical compounds in the air, work in combination with a weather station to provide real-time data on the concentrations that are coming from each facility based off the wind patterns.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: This has put an end to finger pointing about who's to blame each time a smell sparks complaints, says Jacobus.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Smithfield Foods, which operates a meat processing in Des Moines, says it has invested $2m to install a regenerative thermal oxidiser that destroys the chemicals associated with bad smells.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Even so, the company says it does not believe it is the source of odour complaints.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Before installing the monitors – which some local companies help pay for – officials in Des Moines would drive out to the source of a complaint to sniff the air.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Relying on the human nose to sniff out industrial smells is still commonplace.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Claudia Barrios Obregón from Kunak, the company behind the monitors in Des Moines, says: "Right now, the way that cities control or measure odours is olfactometry: a human panel measures and gives an opinion of what the odour is like.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: But that's not that realistic." The Spanish company's monitors are an example of so-called electronic noses that make it easier to detect smells.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Whatever technology is used, it can be hard to keep everyone happy, as smells are so subjective.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "Unfortunately, the general rule is that the nastier we perceive the odour to be, the more sensitive towards it we are," says Johan Lundström, a professor in the science of smell at the Karolinska Institute in Stockholm, Sweden.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Rainmaker's drones were used over Alaska this year On 23 August, Cooper Freeman had no idea clouds above his head were being filled with a silver compound in order to cause rainfall.

sentences.text: Those crystals eventually become large enough to fall as rain or snow, depending on the temperatures below.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Essentially, cloud seeding speeds up the natural process of water vapor condensing inside of clouds.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Eddie Lever was able to leave his tenancy more easily because of the Renters' Rights Act When the Renters' Rights Act came into force in May it was described as the biggest change for tenants in England in a generation, giving more stability and security to the millions of people who rent from private landlords.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: The legislation has also prompted a shake-up of the student rental market, which has posed challenges for landlords as it allows people to leave a tenancy rather than being tied in for the full academic year.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Eddie Lever had finished his first year at the University of Exeter when he decided the course wasn't for him.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: The 20-year-old wanted to switch to studying international relations at the University of York but had already organised his house for the upcoming year.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: The tenancy was signed and had started.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: But because of changes in the Renters' Rights Act, Eddie only had to give two months' notice before he could leave and stop paying rent.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: The legislation ended fixed-term tenancies - where renters are tied in to contracts for a specific number of months.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: For students, previously contracts were generally for the full academic year.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Instead, properties are now rented on a rolling basis, which means tenants pay rent weekly or monthly with no fixed end date.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: University-owned halls of residence and Purpose-Built Student Accommodation are exempt , external and can still offer fixed-term contracts so this change primarily affects students renting from a private landlord.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: "If the Renters' Rights Act wasn't a thing, I don't think I would have been able to move universities because I would have been locked into the full [year] contract," Eddie explains.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Fortunately, Eddie had a friend who was looking for a room who was able to take his place so his housemates could sign a new tenancy.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: He acknowledges the situation would have been more difficult for his housemates if there wasn't someone who could take his room.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: However, Eddie thinks the benefits for students are worth this risk.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: "If you were to fall out with your flatmates or if you decide that university is not for you, being locked into a full-term contract can be really prohibitive financially," he says.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: "So without that flexibility, people can really be locked into situations that they don't necessarily want to be in." Lewis Wilson, vice president for higher education at the National Union of Students, says this flexibility means students can also save money on rent by moving home for the summer.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: While previously, many student rental contracts ran into the summer after courses had finished, students can now choose to move out earlier if they want.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Wilson says students also benefit from wider changes in the act, which bans landlords in England from evicting tenants without a reason.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Campaigners argue this gives renters greater security and confidence to ask for repairs, without fearing they could be evicted if they raise concerns.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Lewis Wilson from the NUS says the legislation has given students more freedom to move out when they want However, greater flexibility for students to leave tenancies also means less certainty for landlords.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: The act did introduce a specific ground , external for landlords to evict a group of students at the end of the academic year if they intend to re-let the property to students.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Chris Norris, chief policy officer at the National Residential Landlords Association, says the bigger problem for student landlords is if their tenants choose to move out earlier.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: He argues this is a bigger risk for students - who may fall out with their housemates or drop out of university - than, for example, families, who are less likely to want to move out after just a few months.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Norris says the end of fixed-term tenancies means student houses could be left empty over the summer after courses finish - or even earlier.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: He adds that it is now more difficult for student landlords to rent a house for just a few months as they don't know how long the tenants will stay and can't guarantee it will be available for students again in the autumn.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Norris says it's early days for the new legislation and many landlords are taking this year as a test to see how these issues play out in practice.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: However, he warns that some may choose to increase the monthly rent they charge to cover the risk of their properties being empty over the summer.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: In some cases, he says landlords may even sell up or stop renting to students, reducing supply and pushing up prices.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Sue Lawes thinks the changes mean many student landlords will put up their rent Sue Lawes, who rents three shared houses to students in Norwich, is worried about the changes.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: While Sue says she doesn't want to put up her prices, if her houses end up being empty over the summer because students decide to end their tenancy after their final exams she says she may have to.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: She has already brought forward the start of her tenancy agreements to August instead of September to try and reduce the risks of this.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: However, she says if her tenants move out earlier in the year she would struggle to make a profit, whilst covering costs including her mortgage, council tax and utility standing charges when the properties are empty.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: She argues higher monthly rents would mean bigger upfront costs for students and higher overall costs for those who do choose to carry on renting over the summer.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Sue stresses that she supports the aim of the legislation to give tenants greater security and that students should be able to move out if their landlord is not carrying out repairs.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: But she wants landlords to be allowed to offer fixed-term contracts to students in line with the academic year to avoid properties being left empty over the summer.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: "Landlords are going to find it very, very hard to absorb those void periods," she says.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: "Landlords will put prices up and students are going to pay." Sign up for our Politics Essential newsletter to keep up with the inner workings of Westminster and beyond.

sentences.text: There are several issues on the horizon for the prime minister This feels like the week where the rubber hits the road for the prime minister's new government.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham faces crunch decisions in his next 100 days

sentences.text: It is now 100 days since Andy Burnham arrived in Downing Street from Buckingham Palace and began to assemble his cabinet.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham faces crunch decisions in his next 100 days

sentences.text: Three months later, Labour MPs are more chipper, the party's poll ratings have notched up and the tone and style of government feels very different from when Sir Keir Starmer was in charge.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham faces crunch decisions in his next 100 days

sentences.text: Coming next, though, there are a whole series of crunchy decisions and trade offs – economic and political – some of which are inevitable and some of which Burnham has decided to lean into.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham faces crunch decisions in his next 100 days

sentences.text: You would be forgiven for only just clocking there is a Budget this week.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham faces crunch decisions in his next 100 days

sentences.text: There are three reasons for this year's feeling like a comparatively low key affair: it is happening a month earlier than a year ago, squeezing the space available for briefings, leaks and speculation.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham faces crunch decisions in his next 100 days

sentences.text: It is considerably smaller in big picture terms – in other words the scale of tax rises – so limiting the noisy talk in advance about who might get clobbered.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham faces crunch decisions in his next 100 days

sentences.text: And the new chancellor John Healey and his team have sought to make a virtue out of not saying very much beforehand.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham faces crunch decisions in his next 100 days

sentences.text: But woe betide suggesting to anyone involved in assembling this Budget that it is a steady-as-she-goes, nothing-to-see-here thing.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham faces crunch decisions in his next 100 days

sentences.text: Every Budget is a big deal, goes the argument run past me by some.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham faces crunch decisions in his next 100 days

sentences.text: They don't all have to be visible from space in the way some recent ones have been – think Kwasi Kwarteng in one direction followed by Jeremy Hunt in the other four years ago, or Rachel Reeves in the last two years.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham faces crunch decisions in his next 100 days

sentences.text: Cost of living support for some, help for entrepreneurs, more financial clout for mayors in England and an economy now recuperating will be themes for Healey on Wednesday.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham faces crunch decisions in his next 100 days

sentences.text: You will be the judge of this Budget's scale – its value, or the lack of it to you – before long.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham faces crunch decisions in his next 100 days

sentences.text: In recent years, many but not all politicians have approached the issue of Brexit like you or I might approach an electric fence.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham faces crunch decisions in his next 100 days

sentences.text: Avoid getting too close and, if needs must, climb over it gingerly.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham faces crunch decisions in his next 100 days

sentences.text: Burnham has no such reservations: he has repeatedly said in the last few weeks, let's talk about Brexit.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham faces crunch decisions in his next 100 days

sentences.text: He reckons the current deal between the UK and European Union isn't good enough.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham faces crunch decisions in his next 100 days

sentences.text: Over the weekend he went further, suggesting he wanted an "honest discussion" about freedom of movement.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham faces crunch decisions in his next 100 days

sentences.text: Countries in the EU's single market have to sign up to freedom of movement, which lets people live and work in all the countries that are part of it.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham faces crunch decisions in his next 100 days

sentences.text: Given how big a deal immigration was for many in the EU referendum in 2016, even reopening the question of freedom of movement feels like a big deal.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham faces crunch decisions in his next 100 days

sentences.text: On Monday morning, the prime minister appeared to add more detail, suggesting freedom of movement would only return in the UK having been sanctioned in a referendum.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham faces crunch decisions in his next 100 days

sentences.text: Later, though, his team wouldn't repeat that , instead emphasising that Burnham wants to start a broad based conversation – without at this point committing to any possible outcome.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham faces crunch decisions in his next 100 days

sentences.text: Some of his MPs felt this was a self-inflicted tangle he could have done without.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham faces crunch decisions in his next 100 days

sentences.text: Others see merit in Burnham's penchant for narrating his thoughts and possible direction publicly, thereby using his position to seek to dominate the political debate.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham faces crunch decisions in his next 100 days

sentences.text: While the Labour Party's centre of gravity tilts towards a collective instinct that a closer relationship with the EU would be preferable to the status quo, there are differences of emphasis and indeed outright disagreements about how much closer and when would be wise.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham faces crunch decisions in his next 100 days

sentences.text: A nod to that scepticism appeared to come publicly from Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood who noted that a call for an honest discussion is "not the same as settled policy".
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham faces crunch decisions in his next 100 days

sentences.text: She added: "The prime minister has also observed that there were very significant issues with freedom of movement when we were within the EU.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham faces crunch decisions in his next 100 days

sentences.text: An honest debate means actually being honest about all of the aspects of that debate and not cherry-picking." Next month, there will be a UK-EU Summit in Brussels, which was due to happen in the summer but was postponed when Sir Keir Starmer resigned.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham faces crunch decisions in his next 100 days

sentences.text: We can expect both sides to talk up tweaks to the current deal and the government to also, in time, set out options for what the long term relationship might look like.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham faces crunch decisions in his next 100 days

sentences.text: On the detail, there are divisions from the cabinet and down.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham faces crunch decisions in his next 100 days

sentences.text: The key thing will be what the party decides to include or not in its next general election manifesto.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham faces crunch decisions in his next 100 days

sentences.text: Last week, Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh approved drilling in the Jackdaw field in the North Sea, about 150 miles east of Aberdeen.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham faces crunch decisions in his next 100 days

sentences.text: This is principally a gas field and Fahnbulleh grounded her justification in providing the UK with greater energy security, at a time of war in Ukraine and in the Middle East.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham faces crunch decisions in his next 100 days

sentences.text: The gas, she said, could be tapped into and serve British homes and businesses pretty much straight away, with the tax revenue put into an "energy wealth fund", with the aim being to invest in renewable and low carbon energy projects.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham faces crunch decisions in his next 100 days

sentences.text: But what about the Rosebank field , 80 miles north west of the Shetland islands, with its focus on oil?
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham faces crunch decisions in his next 100 days

sentences.text: Labour figures in and outside government acknowledge this is a much, much harder sell to plenty in their own party and beyond.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham faces crunch decisions in his next 100 days

sentences.text: Some, who want to see the project go ahead, fear that the energy secretary is not likely to be convinced that it should.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham faces crunch decisions in his next 100 days

sentences.text: It is in that context that we should see allies of the chancellor pointedly making it known that he is in favour of it.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham faces crunch decisions in his next 100 days

sentences.text: His public language was quite telling on the day Jackdaw was approved, when he was talking about the Energy Wealth Fund: "It means the extra tax revenues that come from North Sea oil and gas can be directed into developing more clean energy projects for the future." Note his reference to oil.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham faces crunch decisions in his next 100 days

sentences.text: Fahnbulleh said that Rosebank was "a different proposition" to Jackdaw.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham faces crunch decisions in his next 100 days

sentences.text: Can those who worry, in particular, about the emissions from a new oil field, be won over by an argument grounded in this being a geopolitically pragmatic and environmentally credible part of transition to cleaner fuels?
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham faces crunch decisions in his next 100 days

sentences.text: Some Labour MPs hope so, but they know it's a tall order to persuade some, including some in government – which could, if it was approved, raise the question of ministerial resignations.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham faces crunch decisions in his next 100 days

sentences.text: Expected before long, the former Labour cabinet minister Alan Milburn's review into young people and work – and with it a set of suggestions to try to cut the number of young people not in work, education or training and, in time, to try to cut the benefits bill too.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham faces crunch decisions in his next 100 days

sentences.text: Plenty of Labour MPs acknowledge these are nettles that need grabbing, but how many may flinch when presented with the sharper edges of what might be proposed?
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham faces crunch decisions in his next 100 days

sentences.text: Meanwhile, we await where the government eventually ends up on how long migrants should have to wait to claim permanent residence in the UK .
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham faces crunch decisions in his next 100 days

sentences.text: And then, beyond what is set out in the Budget, how ministers will find the money to spend 3% of national income on defence by the end of the decade – and with what trade offs to make that happen.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham faces crunch decisions in his next 100 days

sentences.text: There will be plenty to observe in the second 100 days of Burnham's government and beyond.

sentences.text: Consultant doctors in England are to stage a two-day strike next month in a dispute over pay and working conditions.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: The walkout will begin on 25 November at 06:59 GMT, with consultants staffing emergency care only.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: This is known as Christmas Day cover and is likely to have a major impact on most routine and elective or planned services.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: The announcement comes after talks had been taking place with the government over the past month, following the vote in favour of strike action by British Medical Association members in July.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: Consultants – the most senior doctors in hospitals – were given a 3.5% pay increase this year.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: But the BMA argues pay has fallen by a quarter over the past 17 years, once inflation is taken into account.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: The union also wants a reduction in the standard working week, from 40 to 35 hours, and higher pay for out-of-hours work, alongside changes to pensions, including greater flexibility over when they can be taken.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: In a joint statement, BMA consultants committee co-chairs Dr Helen Neary and Dr Shanu Datta, said they had tried to negotiate with the government in "good faith", but "time-and-time again ministers have kicked the can down the road".
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: "Unfortunately, that road has now run out, and we have been forced to announce strikes.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: "Consultants take their responsibilities incredibly seriously, and striking does not come naturally, but we are hearing loud and clear from the profession that they have had enough." Average earnings for consultants top £150,000 a year.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: Basic pay starts at £113,500, with the most experienced getting £150,500.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: But many earn tens of thousands in extra payments and awards.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: In the strike ballot, 76% of consultants who took part voted in favour of strike action, with just over half of eligible BMA members taking part.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: The government says this represents only around one in five consultants employed by the NHS in England voting for strike action, as nearly half are not BMA members.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: Health Secretary Yvette Cooper said the government had been in "constructive discussions" with the BMA so it was "disappointing" the strike dates had been announced.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: She said taking strike action would be "irresponsible" and "place the health service under even greater pressure".
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: The strike announcement comes as consultants and other doctors are taking part in strike action during November in Northern Ireland .
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: Consultants last took strike action in England in 2023.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: The long-running dispute involving resident doctors in England came to an end earlier this year after more than three years of on-and-off strike action.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: Do you have three days' worth of food and water in your home?
sentences.article_title: Why should I stockpile and what will I need?

sentences.text: That is what the government has told all of us to have on hand to get through a national emergency, as well as some other basic items.
sentences.article_title: Why should I stockpile and what will I need?

sentences.text: Its "Be Ready" campaign warns that severe weather and cyber attacks could disrupt essential services, and British households need to make sure they have what they need to get through a rocky few days.
sentences.article_title: Why should I stockpile and what will I need?

sentences.text: On Friday, Prime Minister Andy Burnham said unexpected events "seem to becoming more common" and everyone should have "those supplies in the house to get you through those moments".
sentences.article_title: Why should I stockpile and what will I need?

sentences.text: As one expert warns the UK is "light years" behind our neighbours when it comes to preparing for major disruption, we've drilled down into what you need and why.
sentences.article_title: Why should I stockpile and what will I need?

sentences.text: The government recommends having enough supplies in the kitchen to last three days, including bottled water and non-perishable foods.
sentences.article_title: Why should I stockpile and what will I need?

sentences.text: Wet wipes, a torch and cash are also recommended - you can scroll through below to see the full list.
sentences.article_title: Why should I stockpile and what will I need?

sentences.text: Disaster planning expert Professor Lucy Easthope said the goal of asking household to prepare is to make it easier for emergency service to cope in the event of a national emergency.
sentences.article_title: Why should I stockpile and what will I need?

sentences.text: For example, the government says people who need medication should have an extra supply just in case.
sentences.article_title: Why should I stockpile and what will I need?

sentences.text: Prof Easthope says: "If people have got their heart pills for an extra 48 hours, it stops [response crews] from having to immediately find an emergency pharmacist." While the latest government campaign only launched on Thursday, some people are well ahead of the game.
sentences.article_title: Why should I stockpile and what will I need?

sentences.text: Speaking to Radio 5 Live, Bridgette Clamp, who lives in near Penzance in Cornwall, said she has stocked up on "lots of tinned goods" as well as "flour, yeast and everything to bake bread".
sentences.article_title: Why should I stockpile and what will I need?

sentences.text: "We're rocking and rolling," she says.
sentences.article_title: Why should I stockpile and what will I need?

sentences.text: Bridgette says she also bought generators and water pumps following Storm Goretti earlier this year One woman, who spoke to 5 Live anonymously, said she bought "loads and loads" of emergency food - but ended up eating it before it was strictly necessary.
sentences.article_title: Why should I stockpile and what will I need?

sentences.text: Like others, she wondered if the government was "scaremongering", adding: "I don't know but I've certainly bought into it." Rob, who lives off-grid in north Wales, told the programme he has stocked up on so many supplies he "wouldn't even notice" if a disaster struck.
sentences.article_title: Why should I stockpile and what will I need?

sentences.text: But he said he still felt there was "a bit of scaremongering" going on and wondered if he would ever need it all.
sentences.article_title: Why should I stockpile and what will I need?

sentences.text: Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said the advice - which is similar to guidance issued by the previous government - was not triggered by any "particular piece of intelligence", but rather about improving "national resilience" more generally.
sentences.article_title: Why should I stockpile and what will I need?

sentences.text: The government's announcement focused on extreme weather events , which are becoming more frequent because of man-made climate change - but Streeting also referred to the threat of "increasingly sophisticated cyber-attacks" on businesses, and supply chain disruption caused by "hostile state actors or terrorists".
sentences.article_title: Why should I stockpile and what will I need?

sentences.text: Prof Easthope said she has been lobbying the government to launch this sort of campaign for "about 16 years".
sentences.article_title: Why should I stockpile and what will I need?

sentences.text: She said successive governments have been hesitant of "putting out information that might cause tension" - and speculated that this advice may have been "rushed" out ahead of Storm Austen hitting the UK.
sentences.article_title: Why should I stockpile and what will I need?

sentences.text: Expert Prof Lucy Easthope says the UK is playing "massive catch up" to other nations in disaster preparedness While many of us will already have a stash of tinned food in the cupboards, fewer homes are likely to have a store of bottled water.
sentences.article_title: Why should I stockpile and what will I need?

sentences.text: Paul from Torquay, Devon, said to Radio 5 Live: "Who on earth carries three day supply of water?" He added: "I think they've made it our responsibility, rather than their responsibility." Prof Easthope described the UK as "light years" behind neighbouring countries when it comes to preparedness.
sentences.article_title: Why should I stockpile and what will I need?

sentences.text: "Countries like Scandinavia, Denmark, Sweden, Norway, they've been good at this for years," she said.
sentences.article_title: Why should I stockpile and what will I need?

sentences.text: France advises people to store 72-hours' worth of food, while the German government says homes should have enough supplies to last for a 10-day period.
sentences.article_title: Why should I stockpile and what will I need?

sentences.text: "This is one area where I'm very comfortable saying we are playing massive catch-up," added Easthope.
sentences.article_title: Why should I stockpile and what will I need?

sentences.text: Awareness campaigns such as "think 72 hours" make a big difference in the US, Australia and "all around Europe", she said.
sentences.article_title: Why should I stockpile and what will I need?

sentences.text: However, in the UK, she said disaster messaging often gets parodied, or governments are accused of "panic-mongering".
sentences.article_title: Why should I stockpile and what will I need?

sentences.text: "We have seen the pendulum shift" in recent years, she adds, saying that "we are now seeing people recognise this" as an issue that needs tackling.
sentences.article_title: Why should I stockpile and what will I need?
