sentences.article_title: Can you tell ferritin levels from your face?

sentences.text: Lucy says she noticed changes in her skin and hair (left photo) alongside symptoms including fatigue and hair loss when her ferritin levels were low.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: Lighting and shadows also play a part "Do you have ferritin face?" a young woman asks on TikTok, pointing to dark circles, washed-out skin and brittle hair, alongside before-and-after style photographs.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: The content creator puts these features down to her iron levels.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: It is one of a growing number of videos and posts on TikTok and Instagram claiming that low ferritin - a protein which stores iron in the body - can leave visible clues on your face.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: Users list pale or grey-looking skin, dark under-eye circles, dry or cracked lips, hair shedding and weak nails, while others share portraits claiming stark visual differences.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: The phrase "ferritin face" has spread widely across social media, with videos attracting millions of views.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: But doctors say appearance alone cannot diagnose iron deficiency.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: "Ferritin face is not a medical diagnosis," said GP Dr Aziza Sesay, who is based in the West Midlands.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: "However, it may be a clue to tell us that something is going on." Pale skin, hair shedding or brittle nails can accompany low iron, but can also be signs of other conditions, she told BBC News.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: Your ferritin levels show how good your body's iron stores are, while haemoglobin is the protein in red blood cells which carries oxygen.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: When haemoglobin is low, the blood cannot carry as much oxygen - a condition known as anaemia.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: But iron stores can become depleted before that happens, meaning someone can be iron-deficient and have symptoms without being anaemic.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: This video can not be played Can you tell your ferritin levels from your face?
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: "You've got no stored iron but you're maintaining your haemoglobin.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: That's the big disconnect," said consultant haematologist Dr Drew Provan.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: Dr Sue Pavord, also a consultant haematologist, said iron deficiency is common and often under-diagnosed in women.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: UK guidelines from the British Society of Gastroenterology say ferritin below 15 micrograms per litre indicates absent iron stores, while below 30 generally indicates low iron stores.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: Social media users have shared posts and videos claiming that low ferritin can cause visible changes to the face Lucy M, 32, who posts about hair loss as @marvluceskin on Instagram and TikTok, said "ferritin face" seemed to describe changes she had noticed in herself.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: In 2021 she developed heart palpitations, fatigue and hair loss.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: After being told her blood tests were normal and being diagnosed with generalised anxiety disorder, a later test showed her ferritin was 12 micrograms per litre.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: Lucy said she looked "grey" and her hair had become dull and brittle.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: She shared photographs with the BBC from when her ferritin was low, compared to when it had recovered, and said the difference between how she felt and looked was "night and day".
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: Videos about "ferritin face" often encourage viewers to look for a combination of physical signs - from dark circles and pale skin to dry lips, thinning hair and brittle nails - and compare them with their own appearance.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: "You're not ugly, your ferritin is low", one creator says, pointing to the camera.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: Provan said it was "impossible" to determine someone's ferritin levels from how their face looks.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: People who are significantly anaemic may look pale, he explained, while fatigue can contribute to dark circles, but these visual signs are "subjective and unreliable".
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: In people with darker skin, changes in skin colour may be less obvious, Sesay added, meaning someone looking specifically for the signs described online could miss iron deficiency.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: Doctors say appearance alone cannot tell you whether your ferritin is low, and that iron deficiency should be confirmed with a blood test For doctors, symptoms and how someone feels are more useful than appearance.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: Blood tests matter not only to confirm iron deficiency, Provan and Sesay said, but to establish the cause and guide treatment.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: Both said treatment should also address the cause.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: Heavy periods, low dietary iron, gastrointestinal blood loss and problems absorbing iron through the gut can all play a role.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: Iron deficiency is commonly treated with oral iron.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: Pavord said iron tablets are best taken on an empty stomach, ideally first thing in the morning, and advised avoiding tea or coffee around the time they are taken because they can inhibit iron absorption.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: Iron can also be obtained naturally from foods including meat, beans, lentils, leafy green vegetables and fortified cereals.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: Taking iron supplements without a diagnosis can be harmful, while self-treating could delay the investigation of an underlying problem.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: Lucy said social media has nevertheless helped women take symptoms more seriously, and has given some the confidence to ask questions when something feels wrong.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: "There are so many women saying, 'Oh my gosh, this is me," she said, adding that she is not a doctor and presents her content as her own experience.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: For her, doing so has been empowering - giving women information with which to advocate for themselves.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: Sesay called social media a "double-edged sword" - it can encourage people to seek help, but can also lead them to incorrectly diagnose themselves from a short video.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: For Lucy, the useful part is not diagnosing yourself from your appearance, but knowing when something doesn't feel right, and when to ask questions.
sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: Tony Chapman, 75, from Corby in the East Midlands was one of the 1,100 melanoma patients enrolled on the vaccine trial A new personalised cancer vaccine given alongside a widely used immunotherapy drug has cut the risk of patients dying or their skin cancer returning by 42% in a major clinical trial.
sentences.article_title: First personalised cancer vaccine cuts risk of disease returning in major trial

sentences.text: The researchers involved say the results could mark a turning point in cancer treatment, bringing personalised medicine a step closer.
sentences.article_title: First personalised cancer vaccine cuts risk of disease returning in major trial

sentences.text: The trial also found that the new drug combination reduced the risk of melanoma, a type of skin cancer, spreading by 38% over two years compared to immunotherapy alone.
sentences.article_title: First personalised cancer vaccine cuts risk of disease returning in major trial

sentences.text: The drug manufacturers MSD and Moderna say the same approach is already being tested against other tumours, including kidney, bladder and lung cancer.
sentences.article_title: First personalised cancer vaccine cuts risk of disease returning in major trial

sentences.text: Independent cancer experts described the results as impressive but said longer-term studies were still needed to establish whether the treatment really helps most patients live longer, on average.
sentences.article_title: First personalised cancer vaccine cuts risk of disease returning in major trial

sentences.text: The new approach is aimed at cancer patients who have already had their tumour removed through surgery.
sentences.article_title: First personalised cancer vaccine cuts risk of disease returning in major trial

sentences.text: In the trial, 1,137 adults were given Keytruda, an established immunotherapy drug which helps the body's immune system find and attack cancer cells.
sentences.article_title: First personalised cancer vaccine cuts risk of disease returning in major trial

sentences.text: About two-thirds also received an experimental vaccine with the rest being given a placebo or dummy drug.
sentences.article_title: First personalised cancer vaccine cuts risk of disease returning in major trial

sentences.text: The vaccine, called Intismeran, uses the same mRNA technology as some Covid jabs.
sentences.article_title: First personalised cancer vaccine cuts risk of disease returning in major trial

sentences.text: It is personalised to each patient, using information from their own tumour to help train their immune system to recognise cancer cells and target them if they return.
sentences.article_title: First personalised cancer vaccine cuts risk of disease returning in major trial

sentences.text: Two years after starting the treatment, the patients who received the jab were far less likely to have had melanoma come back or see it spread across the body.
sentences.article_title: First personalised cancer vaccine cuts risk of disease returning in major trial

sentences.text: "Personalisation is the next step up and it's really exciting, it's a fabulous technology," says Prof Pippa Corrie, a consultant medical oncologist who helped run part of the study with patients at Addenbrooke's Hospital in Cambridge.
sentences.article_title: First personalised cancer vaccine cuts risk of disease returning in major trial

sentences.text: He had the tumour removed from his chest but a lump later appeared under his arm.
sentences.article_title: First personalised cancer vaccine cuts risk of disease returning in major trial

sentences.text: He was told his cancer had returned and he needed a second operation.
sentences.article_title: First personalised cancer vaccine cuts risk of disease returning in major trial

sentences.text: He then volunteered to take part in the study but, like all the other participants, he still doesn't know whether he was given the experimental vaccine or a placebo alongside his immunotherapy treatment.
sentences.article_title: First personalised cancer vaccine cuts risk of disease returning in major trial

sentences.text: "This just seemed like a really good example of moving science forward, as well as getting some benefit for yourself, so what's to lose?" Tony said.
sentences.article_title: First personalised cancer vaccine cuts risk of disease returning in major trial

sentences.text: Three years on he is now having checks every six months and remains cancer-free.
sentences.article_title: First personalised cancer vaccine cuts risk of disease returning in major trial

sentences.text: Shares in the drugmakers MSD (known as Merck in the US) and Moderna have surged since both companies first hinted at the success of the vaccine in the summer.
sentences.article_title: First personalised cancer vaccine cuts risk of disease returning in major trial

sentences.text: But investors sold off stock on Thursday after financial analysts said the results were not quite as strong as those seen in an earlier, much smaller trial.
sentences.article_title: First personalised cancer vaccine cuts risk of disease returning in major trial

sentences.text: Both companies said they were now "engaging with authorities" suggesting they could file for approval from medicine regulators as soon as next year.
sentences.article_title: First personalised cancer vaccine cuts risk of disease returning in major trial

sentences.text: Widespread NHS use will also depend on cost, given that each individual patient will need to have their tumour genetically analysed and a personalised vaccine made for them.
sentences.article_title: First personalised cancer vaccine cuts risk of disease returning in major trial

sentences.text: The trial will continue so that the patients involved can be monitored – both to see if the cancer returns over time and to assess whether the drug ultimately helps them live longer.
sentences.article_title: First personalised cancer vaccine cuts risk of disease returning in major trial

sentences.text: Professor Alan Melcher from the Institute of Cancer Research in London, who wasn't involved in the research, described the results as "very impressive".
sentences.article_title: First personalised cancer vaccine cuts risk of disease returning in major trial

sentences.text: "It is an important proof of principle for the field, although we shouldn't get ahead of the evidence," he said.
sentences.article_title: First personalised cancer vaccine cuts risk of disease returning in major trial

sentences.text: "We can't assume from one melanoma trial that the same approach will work across all cancers, and longer follow-up will be important to understand the effect on overall survival." The full trial results are due to be presented at the European Society of Medical Oncology (ESMO) cancer conference in Madrid on Saturday.
sentences.article_title: First personalised cancer vaccine cuts risk of disease returning in major trial

sentences.text: They have yet to be published in a peer-reviewed medical journal, where they can be scrutinised by independent experts.

sentences.text: Private companies buying up care homes for older people in England could undermine the government's plan to create a universal care service , the regulator says.
sentences.article_title: Rapid changes to care market risk to National Care Service, regulator says

sentences.text: The Care Quality Commission's annual report , external highlights how a rising share of the care home market is owned by large firms - the five biggest increased their share by 26% in the last two years, driven by interest from US property investors, and now own one in seven homes.
sentences.article_title: Rapid changes to care market risk to National Care Service, regulator says

sentences.text: While there can be benefits, there are concerns the trend can lead to higher prices and a reduction in quality.
sentences.article_title: Rapid changes to care market risk to National Care Service, regulator says

sentences.text: The regulator said rapid changes to the market, including the fragmentation of home help into more smaller services, needed monitoring and clearer planning.
sentences.article_title: Rapid changes to care market risk to National Care Service, regulator says

sentences.text: The CQC said the changes to at-home care, which covers support to help people wash and dress, could create inefficiencies - nearly a third of these services are providing care to four or fewer people.
sentences.article_title: Rapid changes to care market risk to National Care Service, regulator says

sentences.text: In contrast, there are few smaller care homes judged important for providing specialist and personalised care.
sentences.article_title: Rapid changes to care market risk to National Care Service, regulator says

sentences.text: Small care homes have always represented a tiny proportion of the care home market, but over the last 14 years the numbers have fallen significantly, particularly those that combine care with nursing support, which are down by a quarter.
sentences.article_title: Rapid changes to care market risk to National Care Service, regulator says

sentences.text: The CQC said the funding system remains fragile – people using care services either self-fund or, for the poorest, the state helps to pay for their costs.
sentences.article_title: Rapid changes to care market risk to National Care Service, regulator says

sentences.text: And in some areas, providers are increasingly turning to self-funders, making it more difficult for councils to buy the care they need for those relying on state help.
sentences.article_title: Rapid changes to care market risk to National Care Service, regulator says

sentences.text: CQC chief inspector of adult social care Chris Badger said the reshaping of the market was happening "largely by accident rather than design", driven by a combination of economic pressure and the problems some councils were having in buying services for those relying on state-funded care.
sentences.article_title: Rapid changes to care market risk to National Care Service, regulator says

sentences.text: A clinical trial has been launched in the UK which scientists hope could cut years from the search for new treatments for Alzheimer's disease.

sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: "But I was determined that it wasn't going to define me." Angela said she felt empowered joining the trial because "at least you are doing something".
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: "Instead of just sitting there, you're standing up and saying, I will fight back." Alzheimer's is the most common type of dementia, affecting around 600,000 people in the UK.

sentences.text: The AD-SMART study is what's known as a multi-arm, multi-stage platform trial where several treatments are tested simultaneously, with the results compared with one group of participants taking a placebo or dummy.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: Mindy says people often presume she is straight because of her age As a 75-year-old lesbian, Mindy Meleyal has lived through every major milestone in the modern LGBT rights movement, from the start of decriminalisation in 1967 to the first same-sex marriages in 2014.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: But now she says this important part of her identity is frequently overlooked due to her age.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: She's part of England's older LGBTQ+ community, which a new report suggests often experiences poorer health, more limited finances and greater social isolation than the wider older population.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: The report, from the Centre for Ageing Better, says without specialist support, this growing demographic could be forced "back into the closet" when accessing care, warning they may even delay getting the care they need because of concerns about homophobia.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Adam Preston, a housing development manager from the LGBT Foundation charity, says he regularly meets older members of the community in exactly that situation.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "It's very common for people to hide things if they have a carer visiting their home, for example hiding their wedding photos or taking down a trans flag," he says.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Preston is part of the team behind Kindred House, a first-of-its-kind LGBTQ+ social housing scheme for over-55s, set to open in Manchester next year.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: An artist's impression of what Kindred House will look like when it opens The scheme, a joint project with the local council, will provide 80 self-contained apartments and communal areas available to the local community.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: The majority of residents will be LGBTQ+.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: The Kindred House scheme is what's known as extra-care housing, which means residents live independently, but there is a 24/7 care team available for those who need extra help, and all staff will receive specialist training around LGBTQ+ inclusion.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Preston says he hopes the scheme will "trigger some conversations" about how to best support older LGBTQ+ people in the challenges they face.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Mindy and her wife Linda have been together for more than 30 years, but says they're often mistaken for sisters.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "She's 18 inches taller than me, I've got a Yorkshire accent and she's got a Northern Irish accent," Mindy says.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "I think it's pretty obvious we weren't brought up in the same building." She believes part of that is often down to people presuming she is straight because of her age.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "There are different tribes of people in every age group, but when you get older, people start clumping you together with other stereotypes," she says.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: After divorcing her husband and coming out as lesbian, Mindy co-founded a lesbian commune in Hull before moving to Manchester On one occasion, while Mindy was in hospital after a stroke, a nurse referred to Linda as Mindy's husband.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: She said it was not only "insulting", but made her consider what sort of training the staff might have had.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: The Spotlight on Ageing report says these sort of experiences can also have an impact on the support people receive.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Sarah Wilkinson, research and analysis manager at the Centre for Ageing Better, says after a "lifetime of homophobia and transphobia", older LGBTQ+ people now face the "additional, and overlapping, challenge of ageism".
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: The report , external says older LGBTQ+ people are less likely to have children - someone born in 1950 would have been in their 50s by the time same-sex couples could legally adopt - and that they are more likely to be estranged from their families when compared to their heterosexual counterparts.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: The report also found more than half of gay and bisexual men aged 65 and above live alone, compared with less than a quarter of heterosexual men.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Bisexual women aged 50 to 64 are twice as likely as their heterosexual peers to live alone.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: It also suggests that only half of gay and bisexual men aged 50 and above definitely agree they would have someone to help them if they needed, 14 percentage points lower than heterosexual men of the same age.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Norman Goodman, 75, came out as bisexual in his late 60s after the death of his wife Marilyn.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: The couple never had children, and Norman now has no immediate family nearby to help him with things like hospital visits or housework.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: He says his support system comes in the form of his partner Tony, and a group of friends and neighbours he refers to as his "chosen family".
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "I'm lucky, I've got great friends and great neighbours, and I know I can knock on somebody's door day or night and I could get help," he says.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Norman came out as bisexual when he was in his 60s and says he relies on "chosen family" to support him But despite having their support while he's relatively independent, Norman says he worries about the prospect of facing discrimination if he needs more formal care as he ages.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "Hopefully I will maintain and look after myself the best I can, but I've heard horror stories of gay people in nursing homes being treated terribly," he says.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "I think nurses, doctors, carers should all be trained on how to look after LGBT people." It's the reason behind schemes like Manchester's Kindred House, which are not unusual in other parts of the world.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: There are similar projects in Spain, Sweden, Germany, the US and Canada, but in the UK they are few and far between.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: In 2021, the UK's first LGBTQ+ retirement community, Tonic, opened in London with 19 apartments for affordable rental or shared ownership.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: The scheme attracted so much attention, later this year it is set to feature in a Netflix documentary telling the story of one of its first residents, Chek Min-Ong.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: After 43 years together, Min, 77, and his late partner Tim, had discussed their plans for a future where one of them would live alone, as Tim's health deteriorated.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Min and his late partner Tim wanted to make sure they lived somewhere supportive when one of them passed away "Tim and I have always had this very open discussion, we wanted to know, when one of us is not here anymore, the other person will have a community and feel safe," Min says.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: When Tim died five months after moving into Tonic, Min says his new-found community rallied around him.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "It is what [Tim and I] always wanted, that we'd never have to explain ourselves," he says.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "We'd never have to face a question and feel guilty about not telling the full story, or having to lie.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "You're just here, being yourself." While schemes like Kindred House and Tonic are welcomed by Mindy, Norman and Min, the Spotlight on Ageing report warns that, because the older LGBTQ+ population is growing, the demand for specialist services is expected to outstrip supply.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Between 2019 and 2024, the number of over-50s identifying as lesbian, gay or bisexual in the UK increased by around a third - from roughly 340,000 to almost 460,000.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: There was a 4% rise in the number of heterosexual people aged 50 and above in the same period.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: These numbers are projected to continue to increase as the relatively larger younger generations of people identifying as LGBTQ+ age.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Preston warns that without more schemes like Kindred House, and more training and awareness for those in other care settings, the ageing population may struggle to get proper support.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: For Mindy, who is part of a steering group advising on the plans, knowing there may be more options available in the future is reassuring.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "It's important that you can go, that you think, 'You know what, I could live there because I know the staffing, the ethics, the rules, everything about the place has been put together from an LGBTQ+ focus,'" she says.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "That's what we've been doing and it's something I'm really proud of being a part of."
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: As temperatures exceed 30C (86F) in some parts of the UK this week, the last thing people want to do is turn on the oven.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Not only can cooking in hot weather feel like a chore, but many of us find ourselves feeling less hungry altogether.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So when the heat gets too much, should we consider changing our diet?
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Here are three things to think about next time you're hot and hungry.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Cooking chicken in an air fryer uses less than half the energy of a conventional oven "There's no need for more protein in a heatwave," says Aisling Daly, senior lecturer in nutrition at Oxford Brookes University.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But if you fancy it, some of the most common proteins will need cooking (like meat, chicken and fish) and that can be off-putting in the heat.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even an outdoor BBQ can be too hot to handle.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Cooking a chicken leg in the worktop device uses less than half the energy of a conventional oven, according to Radio 4's Sliced Bread .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: And because they are smaller and speedier, they also pump less heat into your kitchen.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But experts say don't forget about your slightly less fashionable slow cooker - likely buried in the back of your cupboard.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even though they run for longer, they're typically more energy efficient and release even less heat than the air fryer.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: That's due to the energy needed by the stomach, intestines and liver to break down and absorb these complex molecules.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So that steak you crave will only bring you out in a sweat.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Franklin was a British chemist and crystallographer, whose X-ray diffraction work helped discover the structure of DNA Rosalind Franklin is the only female scientist named in GCSE and National 5 science exam specifications in the UK, according to new research.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: A Cambridge study found that of the 86 scientists named by UK exam boards, the English chemist, whose work in the 1950s helped reveal the structure of DNA, was the only woman.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Exam specifications set out the skills and knowledge students are expected to have gained by the end of their course and how they will be assessed.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Exam boards said there was "a clear need for greater representation in science qualifications".
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Academics from the University of Cambridge, along with institutions in the US and Australia, examined how many women were mentioned in specifications for biology, chemistry, physics, environmental science, geology and astronomy.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Their work, published in the British Educational Research Journal, looked at six exam boards in the UK: At Key Stage 4 and equivalent, including GCSEs and National 5s in Scotland, Franklin was the only woman among the 86 scientists mentioned.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: She was also one of three women mentioned at Key Stage 5 and equivalent - including A-levels, AS-levels, National Highers and National Advanced Highers - out of a total of 181 scientists.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Marie Tharp, an American cartographer who created the first map of the floor of the Atlantic ocean in the 1950s, and Inge Lehmann, a Danish seismologist who discovered the existence of the Earth's inner core in the 1930s, both feature in the Cambridge OCR's A-­level Geology.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Franklin, who was named in Cambridge OCR's GCSE Biology and Scottish Highers Biology, produced a famous DNA image known as Photograph 51.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Cambridge scientists Francis Crick and James Watson used the image to work out the following year that DNA has a double-helix structure.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Watson, Crick and Franklin's colleague Maurice Wilkins received the 1962 Nobel Prize for the discovery.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Franklin had died four years earlier.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Academics who wrote the paper found that "several major scientific breakthroughs" in specifications were made by women, but they were not explicitly mentioned.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: The paper said: "Many of the scientific discoveries and explanations were developed in the 1800s and early 1900s, a period when scientific and mathematical practice was largely, but not solely, dominated by men.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: "Our findings confirm that the UK science specifications reflect this historical imbalance: although women made significant contributions to major scientific breakthroughs, this fact is rarely acknowledged." The academics recommended that Franklin should be included "in all specifications when teaching DNA structure".
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: They also said specifications should refer to Marie Curie, who discovered radium and polonium and coined the term radioactivity, and nuclear physicist Lise Meitner, who discovered nuclear fission, among others.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: The Department for Education in England said "girls should see the contribution women have made in STEM", adding it was "committed to improving the school curriculum over the coming years, and as part of that will make sure every girl can see where their learning can take them".
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: The Scottish Government said it was "committed to closing the gender gap in STEM and will carefully consider the findings of this research".
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: A million young people are being offered a free meningitis B vaccine.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It comes after concerns over the UK's largest and fastest growing outbreak that happened in Kent earlier this year.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Nearly 90,000 doses of the vaccine have already been given, with 135,000 more booked in for the coming weeks.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: So who needs the vaccine, what's in it and where can you get it for free?
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine offers protection against a dangerous strain of meningitis called meningitis B (MenB) that caused the outbreak in Kent.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine does not contain any live bacteria and cannot cause meningitis.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It is common to get some swelling, redness or tenderness where you have the injection.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: You may also get a mild fever, nausea, headache or muscle aches but these symptoms should disappear after one or two days.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: More serious side effects are rare.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Bookings can be made at high street pharmacies across England.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Seventeen and 18-year-olds can book via the NHS National Booking Service , external if they are already registered with a GP , external .
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Other students under the age of 25 who are heading to a residential college or university this autumn for the first time can also contact a participating pharmacy.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: You do not need to be registered with a GP surgery to use the walk-in service.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Find a participating pharmacy here , external .
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine, given as two doses and at least 28 days apart, is being offered to 17 and 18-year-olds in sixth form and students under the age of 25 who are heading to a residential college or university this autumn for the first time.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Both doses are needed for the fullest protection.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Within weeks, in Kent, there were 29 confirmed or suspected cases and two deaths.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: That's why the new, one-off campaign is being launched - to help protect those at greatest risk and hopefully prevent something like this from happening again.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Students in their first year of university have a risk that is about seven times higher than that of young people of a similar age who do not go to university, says NHS England.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Meningitis infections can be spread through close contact - for example through kissing, sharing vapes and drinks or living in close quarters with a person with the bug.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: UK health officials say the risk to 18-year-olds or those entering university or a residential college for the first time is higher because of increased mixing of social groups and shared accommodation.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: MenB infection can cause serious, life-threatening problems including inflammation of the lining of the brain (meningitis) and blood poisoning (sepsis).
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It can lead to life-changing disabilities such as amputations, hearing loss and brain damage, and in some cases can be fatal.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Vaccination can save lives.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The MenB vaccine was added to the UK NHS childhood immunisation programme for babies born on or after 1 July 2015.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: All babies are now offered it.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: But it means teenagers and young adults over the age of 11 have not received this jab.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Young babies are vaccinated because they are more likely to get invasive infections more often than other age groups, and their bodies are less likely to be able to fight them off.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: However, research suggests the MenB vaccine doesn't necessarily prevent transmission of the infection from person to person, doesn't target all the different B bacteria strains and doesn't provide long-term protection.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: But UK vaccine experts now say government should consider routinely offering the vaccine to all teenagers at around age 15 .
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It will be up to ministers in each nation to decide whether to do this.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Meanwhile, they do want everyone who is eligible to come forward and get the vaccine because it can prevent serious illness.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Around 10,000 people in the Kent region will have already received jabs, as part of the response to the March outbreak.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Each nation has its own plans , external , but all are offering the vaccine to most pupils completing Year 13 or S6 in the summer of 2026 - irrespective of their education plans and including people from this age group who are not currently in school.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Young people aged 18-25 starting university or moving into residential further education settings for the first time in autumn 2026 are also eligible.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: In Wales, those aged 17-18 will receive a letter invite, while those aged 18-25 who are entering higher education will need to contact their health board later in July.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Meningitis can be caused by many different types of viruses or bacteria, which are spread through close contact with a person who has them.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Viral meningitis tends to get better on its own within seven to 10 days.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It can often be treated at home with plenty of rest, painkillers and anti-sickness medicine.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Bacterial meningitis needs to be treated in hospital.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Outbreaks are thankfully rare.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Currently, a separate vaccine covering different strains, the MenACWY vaccine, is offered routinely to 14-year-olds.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The amount of time children in England spend on screens at school could be harming their "physical and developmental health", a group of more than 150 clinicians has warned.
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: GPs, paediatricians and other specialists said in an open letter to Education Secretary Lucy Powell and Health Secretary Yvette Cooper that tablets and laptops are being used without a full understanding of their long-term health impacts, including on eye health.
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: The clinicians said they are prescribing glasses, hearing aids and speech therapy to children "for a problem that is unintentionally being made worse in our schools".
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: The government said it was consulting on screen time guidance for children aged five to 18 but that technology could be a powerful learning tool if used properly.
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: The group of clinicians said nearly one million children are using screens in most lessons, despite studies suggesting a rise in short-sightedness.
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: They pointed to an analysis of 276 studies covering 5.4 million participants around the world.
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: That analysis, they claimed, found a rise in short-sightedness among children and adolescents from around 24% in 1990 to almost 36% by 2023, warning the condition is associated with an increased risk of a range of eye health problems.
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: She told BBC Radio 4's Today programme parents had not been given the chance to "opt out" of the "excessive" use of screens in schools, which risks children "just not thriving" in education.
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: She said an "explosion" in short-sightedness "cannot be put down to genetics alone".
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: It also warned that children with special educational needs are "disproportionately" directed to screen-based learning.
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: Pepe Di'Iasio, general secretary of the Association of School and College Leaders, said education technology can provide schools with "very effective learning tools".
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: But he said such technology was only part of an "overall learning strategy", which also includes classroom discussion and interaction, and that the school day also has  "plenty of non-screen time such as PE, sport, and break times with classmates".
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: "We would welcome the development of practical, evidence-based guidance to support the work of schools in the use of education technology," he added.
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: Paul Whiteman, general secretary of the National Association of Head Teachers, said it was "important that a healthy balance is struck", adding that "greater clarity is needed from the government on this".

sentences.text: A Department for Education spokesperson said the government was developing new screen-time guidance for children aged five to 18, and will consult on the safety of artificial intelligence and educational technology in schools.

sentences.text: Education Secretary Lucy Powell says the government will "update and strengthen" Holocaust education within schools after a major review highlighted the "shocking scale" of antisemitism in British society.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: Schools and colleges in England will be required to recognise antisemitism as a distinct category of harm and take explicit action against it.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: It means anti-Jewish hatred will be treated as a specific safeguarding risk rather than being dealt with through existing measures to stop racism and bullying.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: The government has accepted all of the 27 recommendations made in the government-commissioned review including dedicated training for teachers and more consistent recording of incidents.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: Schools should recognise antisemitism as distinct form of harm, review says The review into antisemitism in schools and colleges in England was led by former Ofsted chief inspector Sir David Bell and presented to Parliament on Wednesday.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: Powell told the BBC it marked a "generational moment" to re-educate young people, among whom she said the issue of antisemitism was "particularly prevalent".
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: She said: "It's definitely a crisis and I think it's actually got worse since Sir David began this review.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: This has become a real challenge for Jewish people in our country, but also Jewish students and Jewish teachers working in our schools and colleges.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: "I do really feel it is a generational moment to educate this generation and the next – that is the job of education – to understand what antisemitism is in the modern world." Speaking on Holocaust education, the education secretary said new lessons will "challenge" some of the concepts that young people have.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: The review also calls for stronger guidance on political impartiality for teachers.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: Powell told the House of Commons "teachers should not bring their own political views into the classroom" but they should not avoid discussing important topics.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: The review was launched following a series of high-profile incidents including the attack at Heaton Park synagogue in Manchester in October 2025, in which two men were killed.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: Separate reviews were also commissioned into antisemitism in healthcare and into public order and hate crime laws.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: The BBC revealed in August that the Bell review had found Jewish schoolchildren were experiencing regular harassment and abuse.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: It also found that headteachers of some Jewish schools were spending more of their time dealing with security arrangements than educational matters .
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: The review also recommends that the government sets up a type of hotline where school leaders can access immediate advice on tackling antisemitism.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: Bell, who is now vice-chancellor of the University of Sunderland, heard evidence from pupils, teachers, governors and parents across state and independent schools, as well as from community organisations.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: He told the BBC: "This is not just a report for Jewish children in Jewish schools.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: This is for all children and young people in all schools and colleges.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: We know that antisemitism crosses all boundaries." Earlier this month, the BBC was given rare access inside a Jewish school in Hertfordshire, where pupils and staff operate under tight security, amid heightened concerns about antisemitism.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: Spencer Lewis, the executive headteacher of Yavneh College, said that security was an "innate part" of his role.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: "When you come in in the morning, there are high gates, high fences, lots of security cameras.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: We have four full-time security staff.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: And it sort of just becomes part of what you do," he said.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: "We think about it a lot." In response to the recommendations, the government will also encourage schools to adopt the International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance (IHRA)'s working definition of antisemitism, although it cannot make it compulsory.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: The definition is supported by mainstream Jewish organisations and has been adopted by 47 countries, including the UK, as well as most British universities.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: However, some of the IHRA definition's examples of antisemitic behaviour have proven controversial.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: The Board of Deputies of British Jews said that adopting the IHRA definition would provide schools with a tool "to deepen understanding of contemporary antisemitism".
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: "Antisemitism in our schools is real, it is widespread, and too often it goes unrecognised and unchallenged." "One-off assemblies are not enough, and neither is sitting pupils in front of a video.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: Young people need the space to ask difficult questions, challenge their own assumptions and understand that antisemitism did not start or end with the Holocaust." The National Education Union raised concerns about creating a "hierarchy of racism" and adopting the IHRA definition.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: It said the latter risked "blurring the line between antisemitism and legitimate criticism of the Israeli government and the genocide in Gaza".
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: The union welcomed a "strengthened focus on antisemitism" while underlining that "no form of racism should be minimised".
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: Recent figures from the Community Security Trust, an organisation which provides security advice and support to the Jewish community, showed a spike in antisemitic incidents at schools.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: Ofcom is investigating whether Meta breached its duties under the UK's online safety laws with the launch of its "Instants" feature on Instagram.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: The tool - allowing users to take and share an instant image with close friends, that disappears once viewed - was launched on Meta's photo-sharing app in May as "a new way to share photos in the moment".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: But the regulator said the social media giant had not properly assessed risks posed by the feature prior to launching it - something it is required to do under the UK's Online Safety Act (OSA).
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: A Meta spokesperson said in a statement that it "takes its regulatory obligations under the Online Safety Act seriously".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "We conducted a risk analysis and briefed Ofcom about this feature on a number of occasions before launching it," they said.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "We will of course co-operate with Ofcom during this investigation." Ofcom said its probe would examine whether Meta breached OSA duties by not carrying out "a suitable and sufficient illegal content risk assessment and children's risk assessment before the launch of Instants".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Under the UK's sweeping online safety rules, platforms including Meta must carry out and update risk assessments to comply with a range of duties, including to tackle illegal content.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: They must also show how they prevent children permitted to use their services from encountering content deemed harmful for them.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: This spans material relating to pornography, or promoting self-harm or suicide - as "priority primary content" - alongside things like abusive, hateful or bullying content.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "Our online safety laws are clear – significant changes to platforms must be risk assessed before they're launched," said Ofcom enforcement director George Lusty.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "This is a vital step that tech firms must take to protect their users," he added.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Images shared with Instants can be viewed by those who have been selected as "close friends" by a user, or those who they follow and are followed back by.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Meta says the feature has a range of built-in protections, including for younger users with Teen Accounts, including preventing screenshots, reshares or forwarding of Instants.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: But disappearing messages and images have been singled out previously as posing particular risks for child or teen users of some apps .
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "Safety by design must be built in, not bolted on, and today's investigation shows we'll take action where we have concerns that providers are failing to comply," Lusty added.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: All three companies have appeared in court this week, arguing they should not need to provide so much information in response to Ofcom's formal requests.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Meta has separately also argued Ofcom should not be able to levy fines for breaches based on its global annual revenue.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: It also contends that its messaging and image-sharing apps should not have to face additional requirements under the OSA, such as tackling paid-for fraud ads.

sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: So I think with disposable nappies it's easier," she said.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: Around one in four children started school in England and Wales last year not fully toilet-trained, and teachers said they have been spending over an hour a day changing nappies, according to the latest research from the children's charity Kindred Squared , external .
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: Felicity Gillespie, chief executive of Kindred Squared, told BBC Radio 4's Today programme that children not being potty trained when starting school was "a real concern for teachers".
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: "They tell us that they're losing, on average across the country, a day a week of teaching time to dealing with potty-training issues." Gillespie is keen to spread the message that "it's best for children to be coming out of nappies" when they are between 18 and 30 months old.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: "When the teacher's leaving the class to change someone's nappy, the rest of the class is having their learning broken up.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: So everybody loses out,” she added.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: The ability to listen to and follow instructions is another skill that helps pupils get the most out of learning when they start reception class Jo Mould, who teaches reception at Robert Wilkinson Primary Academy in York, said she has noticed an improvement in pupils being ready for school this year.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: "We've spent more time teaching in these last three weeks than we have in previous years," she said.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: "The children have come in so ready to learn, because they're more settled and regulated socially and emotionally.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: We've had a really, really positive start to the school year." Jo Mould says not having to deal with toilet training has meant more time spent teaching her pupils York councillor Bob Webb said the impact of the scheme had been "so positive" for both schools and families.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: But he acknowledged a potential "gap in support" for parents between seeing health visitors with their toddler, and the child later arriving at school.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: He said the key to the scheme's success was collaboration across health visitors, schools and other community settings, but that there was "always more that could be done at an earlier age".
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: Twenty local authorities across England have now committed to adopt York's model, developed by Kindred Squared, and use it to encourage earlier potty-training in their areas.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: That means they were assessed by teachers on being able to complete tasks like going to the toilet and paying attention in class.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: The government has said it is still committed to increasing that proportion to 75% by 2028.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: Early Education Minister Paul Waugh said it was "encouraging to see this pilot helping more children develop the confidence and independence they need before starting school", stressing the importance of parents taking early steps towards toilet training.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: In York, Mould said she hopes next year's parents will take on potty-training even earlier.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: "Ideally we'd be at the point where [children] don't need that support when they get here, because they've already been trained by the time they get to us." Do you have any views, comments or questions about this story?
