sentences.text: A woman convinced her former partner she had given birth to two children who most likely did not exist in what a High Court judge described as an "extraordinary" and "elaborate campaign of deceit".
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The man, who has not been named but was referred to as John in the judgement, applied to the Family Court after he was told the woman had sold their two children for a combined £500.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The case heard that the man received messages and photos of the children and paid the woman around £30,000 over the course of two years.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: But in a hearing in February, the woman, who was referred to as Jane, told the judge she had lied about the pregnancies for revenge, claiming the man had abused her.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The court heard the man believed he was the children's' father because in late 2022 his partner told him she was pregnant, sent pictures of an ultrasound image and had become "visibly pregnant" as time went on.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: In May 2023, shortly before the first baby was due, the woman called the police alleging she had been assaulted by the man.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: He was arrested and subsequently held on remand for several months, Mrs Justice Judd said in her ruling which was published on Friday.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: Following this, the woman sent a message to his stepfather saying the baby had been born as well as sharing baby photos.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: At one stage she is said to have sent voice notes to her former partner's mother in the middle of the night with the sound of a baby crying in the background.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: Later, she told the man she was pregnant again and the baby was due in August 2024.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: However, before the due date, the couple split up and did not reconcile.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The woman would go on to tell the man's mother the baby had been born.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The woman admitted to the court she had told him she was pregnant when they were together, and afterwards, but conceded she had told a series of elaborate lies and that there were, in fact, no children.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: She argued she was menopausal at the time and could not have been pregnant and bank statements show she attended a tanning shop on the day she said she had given birth, Mrs Justice Judd said.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: In her judgement, the judge concluded that the "factors that weigh against the children genuinely existing were very strong, stronger than the factors pointing the other way".
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: She said the man was the victim of a "sustained and elaborate campaign of deceit" which also impacted his mother and closest friend.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: "Added to this, the behaviour was cruel, leading a man and his mother to believe they had children and grandchildren respectively.", the Judge said.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The judge added she was unable to conclude the woman's motive for her behaviour but said financial fraud was a "possibility"  and that the "complex mental health problems" she suffered from may have also played a part.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: WhatsApp is introducing new parental controls for teenagers, as tech companies continue to come under pressure to provide more age-appropriate experiences for children.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: The social messaging app's new tools will give parents a range of options, such as being told when their child joins or leaves a group.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: It will also let them decide on privacy settings for their account.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: In a blog post, WhatsApp, clarified parents would not be given the power to see the messages their teen is sending and receiving, which along with calls would stay private and protected by end-to-end encryption.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: And it said the controls were optional, which social media analyst Matt Navarra called an "obvious weakness".
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: He said the move was "fairly convenient" for Meta, which owns WhatsApp, because it reduced the company's reliance on age verification by putting some responsibility on parents and teenagers.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: "Meta is trying to show regulators we have a child safety system, we have parental controls and we're rolling it out across our platforms," he said.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: "I think the big unanswered question is whether enough families will actually use it." The minimum age to use WhatsApp is 13 in the UK, although it is higher in some countries.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: According to the firm, parents will be able to adjust or switch off the controls at any time.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: The settings will be "straightforward to set up" using a Pin set by a parent, which teens will need if they want to switch off the controls.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: Some of the new privacy tools include selecting who can see a child's profile photo and who can add them to groups.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: Parents can also choose how their teenager uses Channels, which allows organisations and public figures to send out content.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: And they will have the option of choosing between the default 13+ setting for Meta AI, the app's optional built-in AI assistant, or a stricter "Limited Content" option.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: "All of these controls are being designed to support open conversations about how to use WhatsApp between parents and teens, while keeping everyone's personal messages private," the company said.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: The changes come as pressure mounts on tech companies from governments and regulators to change the way they operate in order to better protect children using their platforms.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: In June, the government announced it plans to ban under-16s from social media platforms, with the restrictions expected to come into force in March 2027.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: It said "highly effective age assurance" measures would be used to check the age of those using social media.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: WhatsApp is currently excluded from the ban because the government considers it a messaging service.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: Cases of antisemitism affecting university students and staff in the UK increased in the last academic year, according to a charity that monitors antisemitic incidents.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: The Community Security Trust (CST) said it had recorded 95 "university-related" incidents in the 2025-26 academic year - up from 83 the year before.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: It said the number had fallen from its peak in the year after Hamas attacked Israel on 7 October 2023 and the war in Gaza began, but remains "substantially higher" than before that point.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Universities UK (UUK) represents more than 140 institutions and said its members needed to "protect Jewish students and staff", adding that the findings were a "serious concern".
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Lucy Powell, education secretary in England, said the findings in the CST report were "deeply troubling".
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: "We expect universities to take a zero-tolerance approach to antisemitism, and are providing training to help university staff identify and respond to incidents swiftly," she said.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: The CST defines an antisemitic incident as "university-related" if it concerns a student, member of staff or academic at a UK university "in their academic or student capacity" - including on campus and online.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: In 2022-23, the last academic year before the 7 October attack, the CST recorded 53 incidents.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: That grew to 272 in 2023-24.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: A report from the charity examining the past two academic years says reported incidents fell in 2024-25 and but grew again in 2025-26.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: The most common type of incident recorded by CST over both years was abusive behaviour, including verbal abuse, comments made in person or online and antisemitic graffiti.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Its report said that, for the first time, there were two occurrences of extreme violence in 2024-25.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: It said there were six reported assaults across both years, eight incidents of damage and desecration to Jewish property - five of which were in student accommodation - and ten threats.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Around two-thirds of reported incidents involved antisemitic language or targeting alongside references to Israel, Gaza, Hamas, the 7 October attack, and the subsequent conflicts in the Middle East.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: The war in Gaza was triggered by the Hamas attack on Israel on 7 October 2023 in which about 1,200 people were killed and 251 others taken hostage.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Israel launched a mass military offensive on Gaza in response which has killed around 74,000 people, according to the Hamas-run health ministry.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: He added that universities had "a duty to ensure that Jewish students and staff can study, work and participate on campus the same as anyone else".
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Raphi Leon, president of the Union of Jewish Students, said the report "must be a shot in the arm to boost action to support Jewish students and tackle antisemitism".
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Vivienne Stern, chief executive of UUK, said: "The rise in antisemitic incidents in the UK, including on university campuses, is a serious concern.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Children should be introduced to the world of work at the start of primary school, says the author of a major report into youth activity in the UK.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Former minister Alan Milburn says children as young as four should be learning about different careers, with work experience placements made mandatory for 14- to 16-year-olds.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: However, teaching unions warn of the "significant pressure" already facing primary schools and say practical considerations must ensure all schools have access to the support.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: The latest data from the Office for National Statistics (ONS) suggests 981,000 people aged 16 to 24 in the UK were not in education, employment or training (known as Neet), between April and June 2026.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Milburn told the BBC "in primary school, it's really about opening their eyes and giving them a sense about what is possible".
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Despite a push towards apprenticeships and work experience in Years 10 and 11, for many the journey towards becoming Neet starts well before their 16th birthday.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: As a result, Milburn says children should be introduced to the world of work much earlier in their school journey, with dedicated space in the curriculum to "broaden horizons".
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: The final instalment of Alan Milburn's review into Neets is due to be published this autumn He told the BBC this could be achieved by employers giving talks in primary schools and offering taster sessions to children.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: "It'd be good if employers came into schools and said, 'Look, this is what's going on, these are things that are possible.'" Milburn says that for Key Stage 4 pupils - aged between 14 and 16 - experience must be given in a real workplace with employer feedback.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: "Work experience needs to be mandatory.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: It makes a big difference," he told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Milburn also emphasised the difficulty some young people face when trying to find work experience placements.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: "There are about four in ten people aged 14-16 who aren't getting any work experience at all," he said.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Education is devolved in the UK, so while Milburn's review looks at the picture in all four nations, his recommendations regarding education are specific to England.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Currently in England, careers guidance must be offered to students aged 11-18 and work experience is not statutory.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: The government has said its vision , external is to "guarantee two weeks' worth of work experience for every young person" in England.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: In both Scotland and Wales, career-based learning is already a requirement in schools for students as young as three.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Emma, from Kirklees, has grandchildren in Years 1, 2 and 4 and thinks primary school is too young to be introducing careers talks.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: "In primary school, there is too much trying to get little kids to grow up too quickly," she says.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: "Just let them be little kids.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: I know they have to learn and the world's changing, but still, give them a chance to be kids." But Zoe, another parent, disagrees.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: "I think it's a good idea," she says.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Paul Whiteman, general secretary of school leaders' union National Association of Head Teachers (NAHT), warns of the "significant pressure" already facing primary schools.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: "Whenever new mandatory requirements are proposed, it is important to be clear about what might have to give way to make room for them," he says.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Whiteman also highlights the value of existing programmes such as "Primary Futures", which bring in volunteers from different professions into schools to "challenge stereotypes and raise aspirations".
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: "The earlier young people can begin to make connections between what they learn in school and the possibilities that lie ahead, the better," Whiteman says.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Pepe Di'Iasio, general secretary of the Association of School and College Leaders (ASCL), says having someone come into the classroom can really "enlighten [children's] motivation... and give them that sense of passion for all the opportunities beyond the classroom".
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Although he acknowledges that finding opportunities in rural areas could be more challenging.

sentences.text: New vocational GCSEs will be introduced from 2029 for 14-year-olds alongside existing core academic subjects in England.
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: The new subjects could include building and construction, business management and finance, and child development.
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: Education Secretary Lucy Powell said there was "no question" that academic learning was at "the core of any education system", but said there was "huge demand" for subjects with more practical elements too.
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: Education unions said the ideas were welcome, but a clear strategy was needed to make them happen.
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: The Conservatives said the plans risked "throwing away" progress made in recent years.
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: Standards for the new qualifications will be set nationally by the regulator Ofqual to ensure grades are in line with other GCSEs, and will gradually replace other qualifications at this level such as BTec tech awards.
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: The vocational GCSEs will be designed to allow teenagers to progress at 16 to studying similar courses at college, including the new V-levels , which schools and colleges are teaching from autumn 2027, and T-levels .
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: The idea is to create a clear pathway for teenagers into different types of work through a ladder of qualifications.
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: But the Liberal Democrats warned the new vocational GCSEs should not become a "pipeline" directing disadvantaged pupils away from more academic subjects.
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: Powell told the BBC she was "not going to oversee a two-tier education system".
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: "I want working class, disadvantaged young people to have every opportunity to achieve highly academically," she said.
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: Asked whether there would be dedicated funding to help schools cover the cost of the new qualifications, she said the government would "work with the sector to make sure this is absolutely deliverable", and that ministers would "make sure any funding needed is made available".
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: A new national target for employers to help create 200,000 work experience opportunities for under-16s is also being set by Prime Minister Andy Burnham, as part of reforms to shake-up the education system to better prepare young people for the world of work.

sentences.text: Both Queen's University Belfast and Ulster University are expected to have financial deficits in 2025/26 Northern Ireland's universities are facing a "substantial" cut of £21m in the Stormont funding they receive to teach students.

"It's a possibility," Snowden told the committee.

sentences.text: Elon Musk has spent years building Tesla and SpaceX into a pair of trillion-dollar technology empires.
sentences.article_title: Why is Elon Musk plotting a mega-merger of SpaceX and Tesla?

sentences.article_title: Why is Elon Musk plotting a mega-merger of SpaceX and Tesla?

sentences.text: Musk said special committees have been formed to assess a potential deal, although he stressed that there is no guarantee a merger will happen and that nothing has been agreed.
sentences.article_title: Why is Elon Musk plotting a mega-merger of SpaceX and Tesla?

sentences.text: With Tesla valued at roughly $1.5 trillion (£1.1 trillion) and SpaceX at $2 trillion, a combination of the two companies would mark the largest merger ever.
sentences.article_title: Why is Elon Musk plotting a mega-merger of SpaceX and Tesla?

sentences.text: Any deal would also need shareholder backing.
sentences.article_title: Why is Elon Musk plotting a mega-merger of SpaceX and Tesla?

sentences.text: But Musk said he saw "a lot to be gained" in bringing the businesses together.
sentences.article_title: Why is Elon Musk plotting a mega-merger of SpaceX and Tesla?

sentences.text: It's just a question of when," says David Nicholson, chief technology advisor at market research firm The Futurum Group.
sentences.article_title: Why is Elon Musk plotting a mega-merger of SpaceX and Tesla?

sentences.text: During Tesla's earnings call on Wednesday, Musk said he had nothing further to add about the prospect of a merger but quipped: "I feel like I'm tap-dancing through a minefield." Musk said that calling the merger a certainty would be "overstating" things.
sentences.article_title: Why is Elon Musk plotting a mega-merger of SpaceX and Tesla?

sentences.article_title: Why is Elon Musk plotting a mega-merger of SpaceX and Tesla?

sentences.text: The unveiling of the Tesla Roadster last week - a futuristic electric car powered by SpaceX rocket thrusters - served as a "symbolic embodiment" hinting at the two Musk companies merging, Nicholson said.
sentences.article_title: Why is Elon Musk plotting a mega-merger of SpaceX and Tesla?

sentences.text: Musk, chief executive of both SpaceX and Tesla, said bringing the firms together would be beneficial given the work each does around chips, artificial intelligence (AI) and other technology projects.
sentences.article_title: Why is Elon Musk plotting a mega-merger of SpaceX and Tesla?

sentences.text: Specifically, the deal would combine Tesla's cars, robots and self-driving technology with SpaceX's rockets, data centres, satellites and telecommunications operations.
sentences.article_title: Why is Elon Musk plotting a mega-merger of SpaceX and Tesla?

sentences.text: The move could be a step towards Musk's mission to build a self-sustaining city on Mars - a vision that has invited sceptics but also plenty of backers.
sentences.article_title: Why is Elon Musk plotting a mega-merger of SpaceX and Tesla?

sentences.text: Over the past year, Musk has moved to consolidate his businesses, with SpaceX acquiring xAI and X, formerly Twitter, before going public this year.
sentences.article_title: Why is Elon Musk plotting a mega-merger of SpaceX and Tesla?

sentences.article_title: Why is Elon Musk plotting a mega-merger of SpaceX and Tesla?

sentences.article_title: Why is Elon Musk plotting a mega-merger of SpaceX and Tesla?

sentences.article_title: Why is Elon Musk plotting a mega-merger of SpaceX and Tesla?

sentences.article_title: Why is Elon Musk plotting a mega-merger of SpaceX and Tesla?

sentences.text: Students at Ysgol Cemaes, on Anglesey, were able to put their questions to Frank Rubio on Wednesday, who is set to be part of the crew for the Artemis III mission .

sentences.text: During the virtual session, pupils asked him about his experiences of living and working in space, as well as the challenges and excitement of space travel.
sentences.article_title: Pupils who designed a badge sent to space meet NASA astronaut

sentences.text: Astronaut Frank Rubio was stranded on the ISS for 371 days This is not the first time pupils at the primary school have had the chance to speak with astronauts.
sentences.article_title: Pupils who designed a badge sent to space meet NASA astronaut

sentences.text: Earlier this year, they took part in a project to design a badge that was sent into space, later seeing it float in zero gravity aboard the ISS.
sentences.article_title: Pupils who designed a badge sent to space meet NASA astronaut

sentences.text: The opportunity was made possible by former pupil Dr Melanie Coathup - a scientist who works closely with astronauts and has helped inspire the school's growing links with the space industry.

sentences.text: Guto Rhys, acting headteacher, said the students were "extremely excited" ahead of the meeting, and had "been looking at videos of life on the ISS and life in space".
sentences.article_title: Pupils who designed a badge sent to space meet NASA astronaut

sentences.text: The school's headteacher says the pupils were very excited to talk to an astronaut The pupils had prepared many questions to ask Rubio.
sentences.article_title: Pupils who designed a badge sent to space meet NASA astronaut

sentences.text: Harry, 9 and his friend Sofia, 8, were among those listening to the astronaut talk about his experiences.
sentences.article_title: Pupils who designed a badge sent to space meet NASA astronaut

sentences.text: Harry said: "The most interesting thing I've done today is learning about NASA and Frank Rubio." The pupils had been busy preparing in the classroom ahead of the meeting, according to Sofia.

sentences.text: She said: "In the school today, we've been learning about Frank Rubio.
sentences.article_title: Pupils who designed a badge sent to space meet NASA astronaut

sentences.text: We learned that if you're sick in space, there are medical kits to help.
sentences.article_title: Pupils who designed a badge sent to space meet NASA astronaut

sentences.text: "We've been watching some videos about how to brush your teeth and sleep in space." Harry and Sofia were both delighted to meet Frank Rubio Lola, 9, was also in the hall for the talk on Wednesday.
sentences.article_title: Pupils who designed a badge sent to space meet NASA astronaut

sentences.text: She was delighted to see Rubio holding a badge that one of the pupils at the school had designed.
sentences.article_title: Pupils who designed a badge sent to space meet NASA astronaut

sentences.text: "We've been learning about Frank Rubio and that he was supposed to stay in space for six months, but he ended up staying there for a year," she said.
sentences.article_title: Pupils who designed a badge sent to space meet NASA astronaut

sentences.text: African diaspora is finding new audiences in a city celebrated for its musical heritage A new sound is taking Bristol's dancefloors by storm.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Driven by rolling log drums, syncopated rhythms and infectious melodies, amapiano and other electronic sounds from across the African diaspora are finding new audiences in a city celebrated for its musical heritage.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Behind these parties is a new generation of black promoters passionate about creating spaces where black people can hear their music, celebrate their cultures and feel like they belong.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: But for some, building these spaces has also meant confronting the familiar challenge of finding spaces where black music and the communities around it are welcomed and not feared.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Unkle Mykel started hosting events to connect to different cultures Bristol-based promoter Unkle Mykel's journey into events began in his own back garden after he moved to Bristol in 2017.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: What started as garden barbecues gradually grew into a way of bringing people together, particularly members of Bristol's black, Asian and minority ethnic communities.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "It's about celebrating our cultures, bringing people into that fold and connecting," says the 32-year-old, who hosts Bristol Barbecue Family and The Aux Social.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Originally from Kenya, Mykel moved to the UK in 2005.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Since then, he has witnessed changes in the visibility of African music.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "There was no Afrobeats on the airwaves," he laughs, recalling his early years in the country, when he says Caribbean reggae, dancehall and soca were more prominent in the musical landscape he encountered.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Now, he sees the growing popularity of genres such as amapiano - a popular South African house music subgenre - as an opportunity to broaden the scene.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "We don't need to pretend to be nobody else, we're just us.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: It just took a while to get there." DJ and promoter Khiah Lou runs amapiano event called Khaya Nights For 30-year-old DJ and promoter Khiah Lou, representation, she says, is central to her work.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Last year she launched Khaya Nights, an event dedicated to amapiano and other African Caribbean electronic dance music.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Having performed internationally, she had seen how other cities had developed a wider range of events celebrating these sounds.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Bristol, she felt, was lagging behind.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Rather than wait for the scene to develop, Khiah decided to help build it herself.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "If we don't do it, who else is going to do it?" she says.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "Young black people are starting to make a way for themselves because I don't think we have a choice." Khiah says these nights provide a place where people can connect with their identities and see their cultures reflected in the city around them.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "At first it seems like it's just a party, but it's so much more than that," she says.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "It's really important for your own self-identity.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: If your community doesn't have events, where do you feel you can go?" "At first it seems like just a party, but it's so much more than that,' says Khiah Tazmin Samuels, who DJs as Azumei, shares those concerns about representation.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: As part of Rushtown, a black-led music collective, Tazmin wants to champion sounds and subcultures from across Africa, Latin America and the Caribbean.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "My main motivation for getting together with people and starting Rushtown came from seeing the lack of representation of black music that black people are currently listening to within the city," says Tazmin.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: She sees encouraging signs, with more black music-focused brands emerging in Bristol.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: But she believes the wider music industry has yet to recognise the value of what these promoters are building.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Tazmin says the wider music industry must recognise the value of black promoters But creating these spaces is not always straightforward.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Khiah says she has struggled to find venues willing to host nights aimed at black audiences.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Although she considers Bristol an inclusive city, her experience as a promoter has revealed a different side of its nightlife.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "I've had some venue owners straight up tell me they're worried about having a black event," she says.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "I feel like black crowds are kind of met with fear, and that's really disheartening." Mykel describes similar tensions, saying that some venues are enthusiastic about hosting his events, only to face objections from people in the surrounding community.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: The Bamboo Club opened in 1966 as a social hub for Bristol's Caribbean community The young promoters' experiences echo a much longer history of black Bristolians having to create their own spaces for music and social life.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Many black people were turned away from existing clubs and bars in Bristol during the 1960s, which led to the creation of  "blues parties", un-licensed house parties where people danced to genres such as ska, reggae and rocksteady.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: In 1966, Tony Bullimore and his Jamaican-born wife Lalel, opened the Bamboo Club, which served as a cultural lifeline for the city's Caribbean community.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Glen Crooks, 70, who used to perform at the Bamboo Club when he was younger, remembers "sneaking in" with his friends when they were young.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "It was the only place that we could have," he recalls.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "Especially all the Caribbean people could go and really have a good time." Rushtown aims to champion a variety of music genres from the African diaspora Marti Burgess, who has been a co-owner of the nightclub Lakota since 1994, says although attitudes have changed over the years, some prejudices remain.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "There is a long history of treating a predominantly black audience as a concern, rather than recognising the audience, creativity and business that a promoter is bringing," she says.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "They should not have to keep proving that black audiences are welcome or commercially worthwhile." Growing up, Marti was surrounded by music.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Her parents went to the blues clubs and attended the Bamboo Club when it hosted artists such as Bob Marley, Desmond Dekker and Johnny Nash.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "It was through listening to the adults' conversations that I came to understand how much those spaces had grown out of exclusion from mainstream venues," she says.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "Latino Fest this summer opened our eyes further to the audiences and musical communities we could welcome," says Marti.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "We want people across the different genres of black music to see Lakota as a venue that is open to them, where they can bring their music and their audiences." Follow BBC Bristol on Facebook , external , X , external and Instagram , external .

sentences.article_title: Davies crossing divide between pitch and boardroom

sentences.text: For over a decade, the Wales and Tottenham Hotspur defender's natural domain has been the high-stakes intensity of Premier League and international football.
sentences.article_title: Davies crossing divide between pitch and boardroom

sentences.text: But in a week when the Football Association of Wales (FAW) is convening to shape the nation's footballing future, Davies is occupying a very different seat at the table.
sentences.article_title: Davies crossing divide between pitch and boardroom

sentences.text: Appointed to the FAW Council in August 2026 as a dedicated representative for Welsh players, the Wales captain hopes to bridge the gap between those who execute the strategy on the pitch and those who draft it in the boardroom.
sentences.article_title: Davies crossing divide between pitch and boardroom

sentences.text: BBC Wales Sport was granted rare access to the FAW council's inner workings at Dragon Park in Newport, where Davies joined fellow executives to discuss the future of Welsh football.
sentences.article_title: Davies crossing divide between pitch and boardroom

sentences.text: The 33-year-old's decision to take on administrative responsibilities alongside a demanding playing schedule comes down to a simple impulse - stewardship.
sentences.article_title: Davies crossing divide between pitch and boardroom

sentences.text: "Firstly, it's an absolute honour and privilege to play football for Wales," he said.
sentences.article_title: Davies crossing divide between pitch and boardroom

sentences.text: "Because of that honour and how much I've loved doing it - and still love doing it - you want to give back in any way you can.
sentences.article_title: Davies crossing divide between pitch and boardroom

sentences.text: "If I can help using my stature and position as a player to help Welsh football, I'm more than happy to do that." Looking around the room, there is the usual entourage of older men in suits.
sentences.article_title: Davies crossing divide between pitch and boardroom

sentences.text: But it's also clear the FAW has undergone a significant structural change in recent years, modernising its model to bring broader expertise to its decision-making.
sentences.article_title: Davies crossing divide between pitch and boardroom

sentences.text: A notable contingent of women and people of previously underrepresented ethnic backgrounds were also present at the meeting.
sentences.article_title: Davies crossing divide between pitch and boardroom

sentences.text: That's not to say that having the more seasoned administrators there is a bad thing.
sentences.article_title: Davies crossing divide between pitch and boardroom

sentences.text: After all, they bring decades of operational knowledge, but having different voices - including Davies' - and direct experience of modern football is a welcome sight.
sentences.article_title: Davies crossing divide between pitch and boardroom

sentences.text: Davies, a Europa League winner and Champions League runner-up with Spurs, acknowledges that dynamic with characteristic modesty, while identifying precisely what he brings to the discussion.
sentences.article_title: Davies crossing divide between pitch and boardroom

sentences.text: "There are a lot of people in that room with a lot of experience that know a lot about what goes on behind the scenes in football," he conceded.
sentences.article_title: Davies crossing divide between pitch and boardroom

sentences.text: "[They] probably know a lot more than I do.
sentences.article_title: Davies crossing divide between pitch and boardroom

sentences.text: But ultimately, I'm here with a player's voice.
sentences.article_title: Davies crossing divide between pitch and boardroom

sentences.text: "I want to see that Welsh football is giving the best opportunity to all players at every level - not just at the professional level like we are, but throughout the Welsh leagues and down to the grassroots as well," he said.
sentences.article_title: Davies crossing divide between pitch and boardroom

sentences.text: "He spoke this morning - and there are quite a lot of people who don't speak in there," Jones highlighted.
sentences.article_title: Davies crossing divide between pitch and boardroom

sentences.text: "You always find in a community of people that some will have louder voices than others, some are quite comfortable standing there and talking, and some aren't.
sentences.article_title: Davies crossing divide between pitch and boardroom

sentences.article_title: Davies crossing divide between pitch and boardroom

sentences.text: "As a professional player, if Ben tables some issue that we would never have found out if we didn't have him on the council, it can keep pushing us to best practice." Mind you, Davies is not your typical professional footballer.

sentences.text: For keen observers of the Welsh game, his transition into governance feels like a natural evolution.
sentences.article_title: Davies crossing divide between pitch and boardroom

sentences.article_title: Davies crossing divide between pitch and boardroom

sentences.article_title: Davies crossing divide between pitch and boardroom

sentences.text: "Ben does some work for Uefa, as I do, and we were together last year at some of the congresses," he added.
sentences.article_title: Davies crossing divide between pitch and boardroom

sentences.text: "I understand his passion and why he wants to be here.
sentences.article_title: Davies crossing divide between pitch and boardroom

sentences.text: It's early days, but I'm expecting big things from him".
sentences.article_title: Davies crossing divide between pitch and boardroom

sentences.text: Ben Davies was present when Uefa president Aleksander Ceferin visited Wales last November Davies has also earned his Uefa A Licence in coaching, which gives him options - on the touchline or in the boardroom - when his playing days are over.
sentences.article_title: Davies crossing divide between pitch and boardroom

sentences.text: "Look, hopefully [retirement] is still quite a few years away," said Davies.
sentences.article_title: Davies crossing divide between pitch and boardroom

sentences.text: I love playing football, and I want to play as long as I can.
sentences.article_title: Davies crossing divide between pitch and boardroom

sentences.text: But you're a long time retired in this game, and I don't see myself just doing nothing after football.
sentences.article_title: Davies crossing divide between pitch and boardroom

sentences.article_title: Davies crossing divide between pitch and boardroom

sentences.article_title: Davies crossing divide between pitch and boardroom

sentences.text: "It's hard to put a nail in it where your future lies," he added.
sentences.article_title: Davies crossing divide between pitch and boardroom

sentences.text: "If something falls on my lap in the coaching world, then maybe that will be my route.
sentences.article_title: Davies crossing divide between pitch and boardroom

sentences.text: "But I want to be able to use my expertise and what I've learned in the best way that it can be, and I don't know what angle that takes after football yet.
sentences.article_title: Davies crossing divide between pitch and boardroom

sentences.text: "I'd like to be someone who maybe, at some point, crosses that divide from a player to the boardroom or a front-office kind of role, because I haven't seen too many players over the years who have done that.

sentences.text: "I think it definitely adds a pretty good perspective when making decisions."

sentences.text: Finlay O'Neill made his England debut in 2025 "If you'd said to me when I was told I couldn't play rugby league again that it's going to be the best thing to ever happen to me, I'd have said 'you're lying'.
sentences.article_title: Chair skills, quick brain - how O'Neill adapted to wheelchair rugby league

sentences.text: But discovering wheelchair rugby league, which is even better, has been a blessing." Rugby league has always been an important part of Finlay O'Neill's life.
sentences.article_title: Chair skills, quick brain - how O'Neill adapted to wheelchair rugby league

sentences.text: When he dislocated a knee while playing in a game at the age of 16, he put it down to the rigours of the sport.
sentences.article_title: Chair skills, quick brain - how O'Neill adapted to wheelchair rugby league

sentences.text: The knee popped back into place but continued to cause issues, leaving the Halifax teenager struggling on the field and with increasing pain off it too.
sentences.article_title: Chair skills, quick brain - how O'Neill adapted to wheelchair rugby league

sentences.text: After extensive medical tests, he was diagnosed with shallow kneecaps and hypermobility.
sentences.article_title: Chair skills, quick brain - how O'Neill adapted to wheelchair rugby league

sentences.text: His sporting hopes seemed to be over.
sentences.article_title: Chair skills, quick brain - how O'Neill adapted to wheelchair rugby league

sentences.text: But after a lot of family encouragement, he transferred his skills to wheelchair rugby league with Halifax Panthers.
sentences.article_title: Chair skills, quick brain - how O'Neill adapted to wheelchair rugby league

sentences.text: Over the past three years, O'Neill has enjoyed a meteoric rise.
sentences.article_title: Chair skills, quick brain - how O'Neill adapted to wheelchair rugby league

sentences.text: Now he is part of the England squad who will be defending their Wheelchair Rugby League World Cup title in Australia.
sentences.article_title: Chair skills, quick brain - how O'Neill adapted to wheelchair rugby league

sentences.text: "I think the first thing that really struck me was how similar the wheelchair game is in many ways to the running game," O'Neill, now 21, tells BBC Sport.
sentences.article_title: Chair skills, quick brain - how O'Neill adapted to wheelchair rugby league

sentences.text: "From playing the running game, I had the rugby brain and skill - the ability to pass and see things happening, but I didn't have the physical skill of being able to move in a wheelchair, as I don't use one in my day-to-day life, and that was a big challenge.
sentences.article_title: Chair skills, quick brain - how O'Neill adapted to wheelchair rugby league

sentences.text: "At the reserve or development level, if you've got good rugby knowledge, you can play the game, but you can't just rely on those skills in the Super League.
sentences.article_title: Chair skills, quick brain - how O'Neill adapted to wheelchair rugby league

sentences.text: You have to learn how to manipulate the chair and move it around the pitch.
sentences.article_title: Chair skills, quick brain - how O'Neill adapted to wheelchair rugby league

sentences.text: "When you're playing a running sport, you just run and you don't really have to think about it, but in the wheelchair game, you've got to think at the same time about moving your chair to where you want to be, catching a ball, passing it and quickly moving on to the next play.
sentences.article_title: Chair skills, quick brain - how O'Neill adapted to wheelchair rugby league

sentences.text: "At my first Super League training session, I was chasing the others, but playing against quick players means you have to get faster.
sentences.article_title: Chair skills, quick brain - how O'Neill adapted to wheelchair rugby league

sentences.text: He was then selected alongside Halifax team-mates Jack Brown and Rob Hawkins in coach Tom Coyd's 10-player squad for the World Cup, to take place in Wollongong, south of Sydney.

sentences.text: England start their campaign against Wales on Friday (04:30 BST) before games against the USA and Ireland.

sentences.article_title: Chair skills, quick brain - how O'Neill adapted to wheelchair rugby league

sentences.text: "Jack and Rob always say they're each other's biggest rivals and I say I'm the one trying to catch them," he says.
sentences.article_title: Chair skills, quick brain - how O'Neill adapted to wheelchair rugby league

Wheelchair rugby league is played with an oval ball, and wheelchair rugby with a round ball Wheelchair rugby league - the sport O'Neill plays - was developed in France as a way of bringing the sport to people with disabilities.
sentences.article_title: Chair skills, quick brain - how O'Neill adapted to wheelchair rugby league

sentences.text: It is fully inclusive, with disabled and non-disabled players able to play on the same team, and follows many of the same conventions as the running game.
sentences.article_title: Chair skills, quick brain - how O'Neill adapted to wheelchair rugby league

sentences.text: Teams of five players have six tackles to score.
sentences.article_title: Chair skills, quick brain - how O'Neill adapted to wheelchair rugby league

sentences.text: Tackles on the ball carrier are made by pulling off an tag attached to each player's shirt.
sentences.article_title: Chair skills, quick brain - how O'Neill adapted to wheelchair rugby league

sentences.text: A try scores four points, with two points for penalties and conversions, which are taken by punching the ball off a tee over the posts.
sentences.article_title: Chair skills, quick brain - how O'Neill adapted to wheelchair rugby league

sentences.text: The game is played with an oval ball and lasts for 80 minutes, with a maximum of two non-disabled and three disabled players allowed on the field at any one time.
sentences.article_title: Chair skills, quick brain - how O'Neill adapted to wheelchair rugby league

sentences.text: Wheelchair rugby - which is part of the Paralympic Games programme, and is also known as murderball - is played by those with specific neurological and physical impairments including tetraplegia, cerebral palsy and amputations.

sentences.text: New Zealand holds a general election every three years and uses a Mixed-Member Proportional system or MMP.
sentences.article_title: New Zealand election 2026: What you need to know

sentences.text: Each voter makes two choices - the representative of their constituency in parliament and a political party.
sentences.article_title: New Zealand election 2026: What you need to know

sentences.text: The candidate in a constituency with the most votes wins and becomes an MP.
sentences.article_title: New Zealand election 2026: What you need to know

sentences.text: Political parties on the other hand must win at least 5% of the total party votes to secure a seat in parliament.
sentences.article_title: New Zealand election 2026: What you need to know

sentences.text: The seats are also allocated proportionately - if a party wins 40% of the total party votes, it will get 40% of the seats alloted for parties.
sentences.article_title: New Zealand election 2026: What you need to know

sentences.text: The New Zealand parliament typically has 120 seats - 71 are allocated to constituencies and the remaining 49 are distributed to parties proportionately.
sentences.article_title: New Zealand election 2026: What you need to know

sentences.text: New Zealand elections rarely result in an outright majority and parties forge coalitions to form a government.
sentences.article_title: New Zealand election 2026: What you need to know

sentences.text: New Zealand adopted the MMP in 1996 to address concerns that small parties were being left out of the vote.
sentences.article_title: New Zealand election 2026: What you need to know

sentences.text: Immigration has always been central to Donald Trump's message.

sentences.text: When he famously stepped onto the golden escalator at Trump Tower to announce his candidacy for his first presidential term in 2015, he accused Mexico of sending drugs and crime north of the border - and it's been a constant rallying cry ever since.
sentences.article_title: Five ways Trump has changed immigration in the US

sentences.text: Some of his first-term ambitions to stem the flow of would-be immigrants were constrained by the courts.
sentences.article_title: Five ways Trump has changed immigration in the US

sentences.text: But restraints have been weaker in his second term, with a more accommodating Supreme Court and tens of billions of additional enforcement money from Congress.
sentences.article_title: Five ways Trump has changed immigration in the US

sentences.text: Who should be allowed to live in the US remains a big issue on the minds of voters in the upcoming midterm elections, which are largely seen as a referendum on the Trump presidency.
sentences.article_title: Five ways Trump has changed immigration in the US

sentences.text: He promised a closed border and mass deportations in his successful 2024 campaign - and few can deny that he's delivered on both.
sentences.article_title: Five ways Trump has changed immigration in the US

sentences.text: But even among those who voted for a tougher stance, there is a concern that the crackdown has gone too far.
sentences.article_title: Five ways Trump has changed immigration in the US

sentences.text: His signature policy has played out in five key ways.
sentences.article_title: Five ways Trump has changed immigration in the US

sentences.text: Crossings exploded during Joe Biden's presidency, with over 4.5 million migrant "encounters" recorded at the southern border in 2023 and 2024 alone, reflecting the massive numbers of people headed north to the US border.
sentences.article_title: Five ways Trump has changed immigration in the US

sentences.text: His administration eventually brought the monthly figures down significantly by restricting asylum claims and removing migrants entering the US illegally without processing.

sentences.text: When Trump returned to office, that stream of migrants became a trickle.
sentences.article_title: Five ways Trump has changed immigration in the US

sentences.text: Border encounters plummeted.
sentences.article_title: Five ways Trump has changed immigration in the US

sentences.text: By the end of Trump's first year in office, the chaotic scenes that had generated headlines around the globe during the Biden administration had largely gone.
sentences.article_title: Five ways Trump has changed immigration in the US

sentences.text: On a trip to the border city of El Paso, Texas, in November 2025, for example, the BBC found quiet streets where there had previously been makeshift camps housing thousands of migrants granted parole in the US to await immigration proceedings.
sentences.article_title: Five ways Trump has changed immigration in the US

sentences.text: To achieve what he often describes as the "most secure" border in US history, the Trump administration has taken an aggressive, multi-pronged approach.

sentences.text: That has included effectively freezing asylum applications at the border, ending "catch and release" of detainees into the US, deploying troops to the border and pressuring Mexico to clamp down on the flow of migrants headed north.
sentences.article_title: Five ways Trump has changed immigration in the US

sentences.text: "The results could not be clearer: strong enforcement works." A vow to build a "big, beautiful wall" at the nearly 2,000-mile (3,218km) US-Mexico border was a signature promise of Trump's 2016 campaign.

sentences.text: Progress on it has speeded up in his second term, boosted by $46.5bn (£34.7bn) in new funding from Trump's "One Big Beautiful" spending bill.
